Jon Rahm Rodríguez (born 10 November 1994) is a Spanish professional golfer. He was the number one golfer in the World Amateur Golf Ranking for a record 60 weeks. He became a pro in 2016. He later became world number 1 in the Official World Golf Ranking by winning the Memorial Tournament in July 2020. In June 2021, Rahm won the U.S. Open and also became the first Spanish golfer to do so. Rahm was born in Barrika, Basque Country. He has some Swiss ancestry. He lives in Scottsdale, Arizona, United States. He married Kelley Cahill, an American, in 2019. The couple have a son.

Jonas Lars Björkman (born March 23, 1972, Alvesta, Sweden) is a Swedish professional male tennis player and former World No. 4 in singles and World No. 1 in doubles. He is as of the 2006 season the oldest player in the ATP Top 100 (singles). He has also played in numerous Wimbledon tournaments.

Jonas Hiller (born February 12, 1982) is a Swiss former professional ice hockey goaltender. He played parts of nine seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Anaheim Ducks and Calgary Flames. Outside of the NHL, Hiller played for HC Davos, HC Lausanne, and EHC Biel of the National League A (NLA). He would also play for HC La Chaux-de-Fonds of the Swiss League. Before playing in the NHL, Hiller played 13 games for HC Lausanne and 3 seasons for HC Davos of the National League A (NLA). Hiller also won Switzerland's championship in 2002, 2005 and 2007, as well as the Spengler Cup in 2004 and 2006 with HC Davos. He was not drafted but he signed a contract with the Anaheim Ducks on May 25, 2007. On September 30, 2007, Hiller made his NHL debut for the Anaheim Ducks defeating the Los Angeles Kings 4–1 in London, England. In his first season with the Ducks, Hiller recorded a 2.06 goals against average (GAA) and.926 save percentage in 23 games. On November 16, 2008, Hiller earned his first NHL shutout when the Ducks defeated the Los Angeles Kings 2–0. Hiller was named as the Ducks starting goaltender for the 2009 NHL Playoffs. On April 16, 2009, he started in his first playoff and he recorded a shutout against the San Jose Sharks with 35 saves. The Ducks were able to eliminate the Sharks in six games but they were defeated by the Detroit Red Wings in seven games in the next round. On January 30, 2010, he signed a four-year extension with the Ducks going throughout the 2013–14 NHL season. In the 2012-13 NHL Season, Hiller was able to help the Ducks place 2nd overall in the Western Conference. In the 2013 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Ducks were eliminated in the first round in a seven game series against the Detroit Red Wings for the second time in five years. On July 1, 2014, Hiller decided to sign a two-year, $4.5 million per year contract as a free agent with the Calgary Flames. On 16 March 2020, Hiller announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey.

Jonah Tali Lomu (12 May 1975 – 18 November 2015) was a New Zealand rugby union player. He had sixty-three caps as an All Black after debuting in 1994. He was thought to be as the first true global superstar of rugby union. He had a huge impact on the game. He was inducted into the International Rugby Hall of Fame on 9 October 2007, and the IRB Hall of Fame on 24 October 2011. He played for several domestic teams, in the Super Rugby, NPC and later the Magners League competitions. These included the Auckland Blues, Chiefs and Hurricanes, and Counties Manukau, Wellington and later North Harbour and Cardiff Blues. He made a comeback after undergoing a kidney transplant in 2004. Lomu died suddenly of kidney failure in Auckland, New Zealand, aged 40.

Jonas Krumrey (born 25 November 2003) is a German professional footballer. He plays as a goalkeeper for Second league club Liefering. His career began with TSV 1860 Rosenheim and FC Bayern München. In 2017 he went on to the Red Bull Salzburg Academy. Then he became 3rd goalkeeper of FC Liefering behind Daniel Antosch and Adam Stejskal. In the 2021-22 season he is the 2nd goalkeeper of Liefering. His debut for FC Liefering was on August 13, 2021. He played versus SKU Amstettenas part of the Starting XI. In January 2023 he moved into Salzburg's Bundesliga squad. On June 14, 2023, he extended his contract there until 2027. In August 2024 he was loaned to Lyngby BK in Denmark.

Jonas Vingegaard Rasmussen (; born 10 December 1996) is a Danish cyclist. He rides for UCI WorldTeam Team Jumbo–Visma. In July 2022, he won the 2022 Tour de France. Vingegaard was born in Thy, Denmark.

Jonas Deichmann, born 15 April 1987 in Stuttgart, is a German athlete. He holds several world records in cycling and endurance. Jonas has done a triathlon around the world covering a distance of 120 long-distance triathlons (about 456 km (~283 miles) of swimming, 21600 km (~13421 miles) of cycling and 5064 km (~3146 miles) running). Before his triathlon around the world, he set several cycling records from Norway to South Africa, Alaska to Argentina, and across Eurasia. Das Limit bin nur ich (2021). Ravir Film. Cape to Cape (2020). Cycled Media. During his journey, he became famous as the "German Forrest Gump". The book about his journey "Das Limit bin nur ich" is a bestseller. Der Schokoriegel Effekt – mit einfachen Mitteln große Ziele erreichen (2023). Gräfe und Unzer Verlag. Das Limit bin nur ich – Der Bildband (2022). Polyglott Verlag. Das Limit bin nur ich: Wie ich als erster Mensch die Welt im Triathlon umrundete (2021). Polyglott Verlag. Cape to Cape: In Rekordzeit mit dem Fahrrad vom Nordkap bis nach Südafrika (2020). Delius Klasing Verlag.

Jonas Winklhofer (born 27 November 2007) is a German footballer. He plays as Goalkeeper for FC Liefering in the 2nd league. Winklhofer began his career at FC Red Bull Salzburg. Starting in the 2021/22 season, he moved through all the age groups at the Salzburg academy. For the 2025/26 season, he was promoted to the squad of the second-division team FC Liefering. He did not make any appearances during his first season. On 31 July 2026, he finally made his debut in the 2. Liga. He started the match against Kapfenberger SV on the opening day of the 2026/27 season.

Jonas Brodin (born 12 July 1993) is a Swedish professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Minnesota Wild of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Brodin played for Färjestad BK of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). Before playing in the NHL, Brodin played three seasons with Färjestad BK of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He was drafted 10th overall by the Minnesota Wild in the 2011 NHL entry draft. On 12 July 2011, Brodin signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Wild. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Houston Aeros. On 25 January 2013, the Wild called him up and Brodin made his NHL debut in a 5–3 loss against the Detroit Red Wings. During the second period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Tom Gilbert goal. On 14 March, Brodin scored his first NHL goal against Semyon Varlamov in a 5–3 win against the Colorado Avalanche. On 12 October 2014, Brodin signed a six-year, $25 million contract to stay with the Wild. On 15 September 2020, Brodin signed a seven-year, $42 million contract to stay with the Wild.

Jonas Røndbjerg (born 31 March 1999) is a Danish professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Røndbjerg played for Rungsted Ishockey Klub of the Metal Ligaen and Växjö Lakers of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). Before playing in the NHL, Røndbjerg played parts of three seasons with Rungsted Seier Capital of the Metal Ligaen and three seasons with the Växjö Lakers of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He was drafted 65rd overall by the Vegas Golden Knights in the 2017 NHL entry draft. On 30 May 2019, Røndbjerg signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Knights. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Chicago Wolves and Henderson Silver Knights. On 14 October 2021, the Knights called him up and Røndbjerg made his NHL debut in a 6–2 loss against the Los Angeles Kings. On 4 November, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Brett Howden goal in a 5–1 win against the Ottawa Senators. On 11 November, Røndbjerg scored his first NHL goal against Cam Talbot and also recorded an assist on a Paul Cotter goal in a 3–2 win against the Minnesota Wild. On 6 July 2025, Røndbjerg signed an three-year, $2 million contract to stay with the Knights. On 1 July 2026, Røndbjerg signed an three-year, $2 million contract to stay with the Knights.

Jonas Siegenthaler (born 6 May 1997) is a Swiss professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the New Jersey Devils of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Washington Capitals. Outside of the NHL, Siegenthaler played for ZSC Lions of the National League. Before playing in the NHL, Siegenthaler played four seasons with ZSC Lions of the National League. He was drafted 57th overall by the Washington Capitals in the 2015 NHL entry draft. On 30 July 2015, Siegenthaler signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Capitals. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Hershey Bears. On 9 November 2018, the Capitals called him up and Siegenthaler made his NHL debut in a 2–1 loss against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On 14 December 2018, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on an Alexander Ovechkin goal in a 6–5 overtime win against the Carolina Hurricanes. On 9 November 2019, Siegenthaler scored his first NHL goal against Marc-André Fleury in a 5–2 win against the Vegas Golden Knights. On 11 April 2021, the Capitals traded Siegenthaler to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for a 2021 conditional third-round draft pick. On 9 July, Siegenthaler signed a two-year, $2.25 million contract to stay with the Devils. On 26 July 2022, Siegenthaler signed a five-year, $17 million contract to stay with the Devils.

Jonah Gadjovich (born October 12, 1998) is a Canadian professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Florida Panthers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Vancouver Canucks and San Jose Sharks. Gadjovich is a two-time Stanley Cup champion, winning back-to-back with the Panthers in 2024 and 2025. Before playing in the NHL, Gadjovich played four seasons with the Owen Sound Attack of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with the Attack. He was named to the Second All-Star Team. He was drafted 55th overall by the Vancouver Canucks of the 2017 NHL entry draft. On October 16, 2017, Gadjovich signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Canucks. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Utica Comets. On May 16, 2021, the Canucks called him up and Gadjovich made his NHL debut in a 6–5 overtime loss against the Calgary Flames. On October 6, 2021, the Canucks placed Gadjovich onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the San Jose Sharks the next day. On October 24, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Jasper Weatherby goal in a 4–3 loss against the Boston Bruins. On February 27, 2022, Gadjovich scored his first NHL goal against Philipp Grubauer in a 3–1 win against the Seattle Kraken. On August 29, 2022, Gadjovich signed a one-year contract to stay with the Sharks. On October 16, 2023, Gadjovich signed a one-year contract to join the Florida Panthers. He helped the Panthers during the playoffs. They defeated the Tampa Bay Lightning, Boston Bruins, and New York Rangers. They went on to defeat the Edmonton Oilers four games to three in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Panthers franchise history. Tkachuk and the Panthers made it back to the Stanley Cup Final the next year where they won their second Stanley Cup in a row. On October 12, 2025, Gadjovich signed a two-year contract to stay with the Panthers.

Jonathan Edwards (theologian) (1703–1758), an American jalen and theologian and president of Princeton University Jonathan Edwards (athlete) (born 1966), a British triple jumper and world record holder

Jonathan David Edwards, CBE, (born 10 May 1966 in London) is a former British triple jumper. He is a former Olympic, Commonwealth, European and World champion. He has held the world record in the event since 1995. After his retirement as an athlete, Edwards has worked as an athletics commentator and presenter for BBC television. He was a devout Christian. He presented episodes of the BBC Christian worship programme Songs of Praise. He lost faith in 2007. He was a member of the London Organising Committee for the Olympic Games in 2012. He is President of the Wenlock Olympian Society. Edwards attended West Buckland School where his ability in the triple jump was seen at an early age. He was a strong all-rounder and on leaving received the school's top award for sporting and academic excellence, the Fortescue Medal. Other students with Edwards at West Buckland School included Victor Ubogu and Steve Ojomoh. Both are former Bath and England Rugby international players. Edwards now has a Sports Hall at West Buckland named after him; The Jonathan Edwards Sports Centre. Edwards then read Physics at Durham University, attending Van Mildert College. Because of his strong Christian beliefs, he refused to compete on Sundays at first. Eventually he decided to do so in 1993. This decision proved important, since the qualifying round at that year's World Championships took place on a Sunday. He went on to win the bronze medal. In his breakthrough year of 1995, he produced a jump of 18.43 m (60 feet 5½ inches) at the European Cup. The leap was wind assisted and did not count for record purposes. But it was a sign of things to come as he capped an unbeaten year. He had a historic gold medal performance at the World Championships. There he broke the world record twice in the same meet. On his first jump, he became the first man to legally pass the 18-metre barrier (18.16 m/59 feet 7 inches). That record lasted for about 20 minutes. His second jump of 18.29 m made him the first to jump 60 feet. During his commentary for the 2008 Summer Olympics, Edwards said that during the 1995 World Championships, he felt as if "he could jump as far as he needed to". Later the same year Edwards became the BBC Sports Personality of the Year. During 1996 Edwards went into the Olympic games as favourite and world record holder. But it was American Kenny Harrison who took the gold with a jump of 18.09 m. Edwards walked away with the silver after a leap of 17.88 m (the longest ever jump not to win gold). Edwards won the gold medal at the 2000 Summer Olympic Games. He was awarded the CBE shortly afterwards. He also won golds at the 2001 World Championships and 2002 Commonwealth Games. At one point in 2002, Edwards held all the gold medals for the "four majors" (Olympic Games, World Championships, Commonwealth Games & European Championships). He retired after the 2003 World Championships as Great Britain's most successful medal winning athlete. Following his retirement, Edwards pursued a media career as a television presenter. He worked mainly for the BBC as a sports commentator and on programmes such as Songs of Praise. He gave up this programme, due to his loss of faith, in February 2007. In 2004 Edwards joined with Paula Radcliffe on an Olympic Special Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?. The pair raised £64,000 for charity with half of that sum going to the British Olympic Association and a quarter of the sum going to Asthma UK. He was a member of the London Organising Committee for the Olympic Games. He represented athletes in the organisation of the 2012 Summer Olympics. He is President of the Wenlock Olympian Soceity. Triple Jump - 18.29 (WR), 18.43 m W +2.4 (not ratified due to excessive wind conditions) An honorary doctorate was conferred upon him at a ceremony at the University of Exeter on 21 January 2006. Later in the same year, an honorary doctorate of the university (DUniv) was conferred upon him at the winter graduation ceremony of the University of Ulster (19 December 2006). Edwards lives with his wife Alison in Gosforth, Newcastle upon Tyne. He has two sons, Nathan and Sam. He initially refused to compete on Sundays due to his devout Christian beliefs. This decision cost him a chance to compete in the 1991 World Championships. However, in 1993, after much thinking and discussion with his father (a vicar), he changed his mind. He decided that God gave him his talent in order for him to compete in athletics. On 2 February 2007 it was widely reported that Edwards had lost his faith in God despite him once saying "My relationship with Jesus and God is fundamental to everything I do. I have made a commitment and dedication in that relationship to serve God in every area of my life." The Daily Mail described Edwards as a "man deeply troubled by the collapse of his Christian faith". It also revealed that a friend said "[Edwards] has a deep, theological comprehension of the Bible, making his spiritual meltdown even more unlikely... They still go to church as a family" The Daily Mail article also quoted Edwards as saying that he is going through a difficult period in his life. A period that is deeply personal to him and his family such that he does not wish to comment on. Edwards presented episodes of the Christian praise show Songs of Praise until 2007. In an interview in The Times on 27 June 2007, Edwards said: "If there is no God, does that mean that life has no purpose? Does it mean that personal existence ends at death? They are thoughts that do my head in. One thing that I can say, however, is that even if I am unable to discover some fundamental purpose to life, this will not give me a reason to return to Christianity. Just because something is unpalatable does not mean that it is not true." Furthermore, in the interview with The Times he also stated "When you think about it rationally, it does seem incredibly improbable that there is a God." In the same interview he also said "I feel internally happier than at any time of my life." Edwards confirmed his rejection of Christianity in an interview on BBC Five Live Sportsweek on 29 July 2007.

Jonathan David González Valencia (3 July 1995 – 19 September 2025) was an Ecuadorian footballer, commonly known as "Speedy Gonzalez". He was capped four times for Ecuador, and played for them at the 2015 Copa América. González was fatally shot in Esmeraldas Province, Ecuador on 19 September 2025, at the age of 30.

Jonatan Berggren (born 16 July 2000) is a Swedish professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the St. Louis Blues of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Detroit Red Wings. Outside of the NHL, Berggren played for Skellefteå AIK of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). Before playing in the NHL, Berggren played parts of four seasons with Skellefteå AIK of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He was drafted 33rd overall by the Detroit Red Wings in the 2018 NHL entry draft. On 20 May 2021, Berggren signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Red Wings. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Grand Rapids Griffins. On 10 November 2022, the Red Wings called him up and Berggren made his NHL debut in a 8–2 loss against the New York Rangers. During the first period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Joe Veleno goal. On 15 November, Berggren scored his first NHL goal against John Gibson in a 3–2 overtime loss against the Anaheim Ducks. On 16 September 2024, Berggren signed a one-year, $825,000 contract to stay with the Wings. On 30 June 2025, Berggren signed a one-year, $1.825 million contract to stay with the Wings. On December 16, 2025, the Red Wings placed Berggren onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the St. Louis Blues the next day.

Jonathan Drouin (born March 28, 1995) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the St. Louis Blues of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Tampa Bay Lightning, Montreal Canadiens, Colorado Avalanche, and New York Islanders. Before playing in the NHL, Drouin played three seasons with the Halifax Mooseheads of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He had a successful time with the Mooseheads. He won the Mike Bossy Trophy for being the top prospect in the QMJHL, the Paul Dumont Trophy for the QMJHL's personality of the year, and the Michel Brière Memorial Trophy for being the QMJHL's most valuable player. He was also named to back-to-back First All-Star Teams. He helped the Mooseheads during the playoffs. They defeated the Saint John Sea Dogs, Gatineau Olympiques, and Rouyn-Noranda Huskies before defeating the Baie-Comeau Drakkar four games to one to win the President's Cup. This earned them a spot in the Memorial Cup tournament. The Mooseheads defeated the Portland Winterhawks 6-4 in the final game to win the first Memorial Cup in Mooseheads franchise history. He was drafted 3rd overall by the Tampa Bay Lightning in the 2013 NHL entry draft. On July 5, 2013, Drouin signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Lightning. He was sent down to play with the AHL-affiliate Syracuse Crunch. On October 20, 2014, the Lightning called him up and Drouin made his NHL debut in a 3–2 loss against the Edmonton Oilers. The next day, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Valtteri Filppula goal in a 2–1 overtime win against the Calgary Flames. Three days after that, Drouin scored his first NHL goal against Ondřej Pavelec in a 4–2 win against the Winnipeg Jets. On June 15, 2017, the Lightning traded Drouin and a 2018 conditional sixth-round draft pick to the Montreal Canadiens in exchange for Mikhail Sergachev and a 2018 conditional second-round draft pick. That same day, Drouin signed a six-year, $33 million contract to stay with the Canadiens. On January 19, 2022, Drouin was fined $5,000.00 by the league after cross-checking Dallas Stars player Tyler Seguin during a game. On July 1, 2023, Drouin signed a one-year, $825,000 contract to join the Colorado Avalanche. He played parts of two seasons with the Avalanche. On July 1, 2025, Drouin signed a two-year, $8 million contract to join the New York Islanders. He scored 3 goals and recorded 18 assists for 21 points in 55 regular seasons games with the Islanders. On March 6, 2026, the Islanders traded Drouin along with Marcus Gidlof, a 2026 first-round draft pick and a 2026 third-round draft pick to the St. Louis Blues in exchange for Brayden Schenn.

Jonathan Penrose OBE (7 October 1933 – 30 November 2021) was an English chess player. FIDE made him a grandmaster in 1993. He competed in Chess Olympiads between 1952 and 1962, and at the Olympiads of 1968 and 1970. His scores included +9−1=7 in 1962 (Varna), and +10−0=5 in 1968 (Lugano). On both occasions he won an individual silver medal on first board. In 1968, his score was bettered only by the World Champion, Tigran Petrosian. Penrose won the British Chess Championship ten times between 1958 and 1969. This is a record. Penrose was awarded the OBE in 1971. He died on 30 November 2021, at the age of 88.

Jonathan Mensah (born 13 July 1990), commonly known simply as Jonathan, is a Ghanaian professional footballer who plays as a defender. He previously played for Ashanti Gold, Free State Stars, Granada, Evian, Anzhi Makhachkala, Columbus Crew, San Jose Earthquakes, and New England Revolution. Jonathan has represented the Ghana national team at two World Cups. To avoid confusion with the similarly named but unrelated John Mensah, he is typically known as and plays with the name "Jonathan" on his shirt. A rugged defender, known for his fierce tackling, man-marking, physical attributes and passing. Regarded as one of the best Ghanaian defenders in African football. Mensah began his career at Ashanti Gold. In 2008, he moved to the South African club Free State Stars. In July 2009, it was reported that Mensah might move to the Greek club Panathinaikos, but later Mensah decided to stay with the South African club. In January 2010, after moving to the Italian club Udinese, he was sent on loan to the Spanish club Granada. On 8 July 2011 he moved to Evian. On 24 February 2016, he signed a 2.5-year contract with Anji. On January 3, 2017, MLS club Columbus Crew announced the signing of Mensah as a designated player. He made his debut in Major League USA on March 4, 2017 in the opening match of the season against the Chicago Fire. On August 26, 2017, in a match against Dallas, he scored his first MLS goal. In January 2018, Crew removed Mensah's designee status to free up a slot outside the salary cap for Milton Valenzuela. Before the start of the 2020 season, Mensah was named team captain. On 22 October 2020, Mensah extended his contract with Crew for several years. At the end of the 2020 season, he was named to the MLS All-Star Team. On February 10, 2023, Jonathan was purchased by the San Jose Earthquakes for $500,000 in general distribution funds - 200,000 guaranteed and 300,000 conditional, 150,000 per year if the player is with the club in the 2024 and 2025 seasons. He made his debut for the Quakes on February 25 in the opening match of the 2023 season against Atlanta United. At the end of the 2023 season, Mensah's contract with the San Jose Earthquakes expired. On January 4, 2024, Mensah joined the New England Revolution as a free agent, signing a one-year contract for the 2024 season, with an option to extend for the 2025 season. He made his debut for the Revolution on 24 February in the opening match of the season against D.C. United. Jonathan was called up for the first time to the Ghana senior team; he made his debut for the Black Stars against Uganda on 31 May 2009. Since 2010, he has been playing for the Ghana national team, took part in the World Cup in South Africa. Jonathan established himself as a central defensive partner for John Mensah. Jonathan established himself as a player of the main squad after the World Cup. On 8 February 2011, he scored his first goal for Ghana in a friendly match against Togo. He was included in the squad for the 2012 Africa Cup of Nations, the last tournament in the even-numbered years before it was postponed to avoid conflicts with the World Cup. Jonathan played 2 matches in the group stage, but lost his place in the starting lineup at the playoff stage. A year later, he was again included in the squad for the 2013 Africa Cup of Nations, along with his teammate Mohammed Rabiu. However, Jonathan played only once in the entire tournament, coming on as a half-time substitute for third place in place of Boye. On 12 May 2014, Jonathan was included in Ghana's 30-man squad for the 2014 FIFA World Cup. On 2 June, he was included in the final line-up. Mensah started every match in the tournament, although Ghana failed to progress from the group and ended the tournament with one draw and two defeats. He was included in the squad for the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations. Jonathan is known to be a devout Christian who reads Psalms before every game. He is friends with fellow Christian footballers Christian Atsu and Odion Ighalo. Columbus Crew SC Humanitarian of the Year: 2017 Columbus Crew SC Defender of the Year: 2018, 2019, 2020

Jonathan Lekkerimäki (born 24 July 2004) is a Swedish professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Vancouver Canucks of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Lekkerimäki played for Djurgårdens IF and Örebro HK of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). Before playing in the NHL, Lekkerimäki played one season with Djurgårdens IF and one season with Örebro HK of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He had a successful time with his teams. He finished the 2023–24 season scoring 19 goals and recording 12 assists for 31 points in 46 regular season games. For his effort, he was named the SHL Rookie of the Year. He was drafted 15th overall by the Vancouver Canucks in the 2022 NHL entry draft. On 6 May 2023, Lekkerimäki signed a three-year, $918,333 entry-level contract to join the Canucks. On 13 January 2021, Lekkerimäki made his NHL debut in a 3–1 win against the Calgary Flames. On 14 November 2024, Lekkerimäki scored his first NHL goal against Semyon Varlamov in a 5–2 loss against the New York Islanders.

Jonathan Marchessault (; born December 27, 1990) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Columbus Blue Jackets, Tampa Bay Lightning, Florida Panthers, and Vegas Golden Knights. Marchessault is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Golden Knights in 2023 and a one-time Conn Smythe Trophy winner in 2023. He is also a one-time All-Star, being named one in 2022. Before playing in the NHL, Marchessault played four seasons with the Quebec Remparts of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He had a successful time with the Remparts, being named to the QMJHL First All-Star Team in 2011. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On July 23, 2015, Marchessault signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Columbus Blue Jackets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Connecticut Whale and Springfield Falcons. On December 11, the Jackets called him up and Marchessault made his NHL debut in a 4–1 loss against the St. Louis Blues. On March 5, 2014, the Jackets traded Marchessault along with Dalton Smith to the Tampa Bay Lightning in exchange for Matt Taormina and Dana Tyrell. On April 11, 2015, Marchessault scored his first NHL goal against Tuukka Rask in a 3–2 win against the Boston Bruins. On June 28, Marchessault signed a one-year, $600,000 contract to stay with the Lightning. On July 1, 2016, Marchessault signed a two-year, $1.5 million contract to join the Florida Panthers. He scored 30 goals and recorded 21 assists for 51 points in 75 regular season games for the Panthers. On March 25, 2017, Marchessault recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 7–0 win against the Chicago Blackhawks. On June 21, 2017, the Panthers left Marchessault unprotected and he was selected by the Vegas Golden Knights in the 2017 NHL expansion draft. On January 3, 2018, Marchessault signed a six-year, $30 million contract to stay with the Knights. He helped the Knights when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Winnipeg Jets, Edmonton Oilers, and Dallas Stars. They went on to defeat the Florida Panthers four games to one in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Hurricanes franchise history. He also won the Conn Smythe Trophy for being the most valuable player in the playoffs and became the first undrafte player since Wayne Gretzky in 1988 to win the award.. On July 1, 2024, Marchessault signed a five-year, $27.5 million contract to join the Nashville Predators.
Jonathan Woodgate (born 22 January 1980) is a former English football player. Middlesbrough Player of the Year: 2006–07 Football League Championship Manager of the Month: December 2019, April 2021

Jonathan Zebina (born 19 July 1978) is a French retired professional footballer. Having started his career as a striker, he played right-back for much of his career before being increasingly used as a centre-back.

Jonathan Bryan Toews (; born April 29, 1988 in Winnipeg, Manitoba) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Winnipeg Jets of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Toews played college hockey for 2 years at the University of North Dakota. During his time there, he contributed 85 points (40 goals, 45 assists), a plus-38 rating and a 56.7% faceoff winning percentage in 76 games. He was also able to help UND reach the NCAA Frozen Four in both 2006 and 2007 and served as their alternate captain during his sophomore season He helped UND win the Broadmoor Cup as WCHA champions and he was also named the West Regional MVP after he tallied five points. Before he went into the 2006 NHL Entry Draft, the NHL Central Scouting Bureau ranked Toews third among North American prospects He was drafted with the 3rd overall pick by the Chicago Blackhawks in the 2006 NHL Entry Draft. When Toews brought the Stanley Cup to his hometown of Winnipeg after the Blackhawks won it, the province of Manitoba named a lake in his honour. It is named Toews Lake and is 150 km north of Flin Flon. During that same day, Toews was given the Keys to the City and the Dakota Community Centre in St. Vital where he first played organized hockey was renamed the Jonathan Toews Community Centre in his honour. WCHA Rookie of the Week (twice in 2005–2006) Manitoba’s Male Athlete of the Year (2007, 2010, 2014) He was nominated for the Calder Memorial Trophy (2008) All-Star selection of the 2010 Olympic Hockey Tournament He became the second-youngest person to win the Conn Smythe Trophy (22 years, 41 days; with only Patrick Roy being younger); he was also the youngest Captain to win the Conn Smythe Trophy. He became the youngest person to gain entry into the Triple Gold Club (22 years, 41 days at time last component was achieved) He was named full captain of an NHL team after only 64 NHL games; became the fourth youngest full captain (Landeskog, Crosby, Vincent Lecavalier) in NHL history and quickest by games. He became one of only six players to win Olympic gold and the Stanley Cup in the same year. Didn't attend because of injury.
Jonathan Michael Paul Spector (born March 1, 1986) is an American former soccer player who played as a defender. He played for the United States national team.
Jonathan Alexander de Guzmán (born 13 September 1987) is a professional footballer who plays as a midfielder for Sparta Rotterdam. Born in Canada, he represented the Netherlands internationally.

Jonathan Soriano Casas (born 24 September 1985 in El Pont de Vilomara i Rocafort, Barcelona, Catalonia) is a former Spanish footballer. He played as forward. He started his career aged 15 in Espanyol Barcelona's second team. With 19 he signed a professional contract and was loaned to the then Segunda División club UD Almería. He returned to Espanyol for the 2006/07 season. Soriano was loaned out again for the second half of the season to Polideportivo Ejido. He spent the 2007/2008 season again at Espanyol and was used regularly for the first time. The first half of the following season he played for Espanyol.In the second half of the season he was on loan for Albacete Balompié. In 2009 Soriano went to FC Barcelona B. With the reserve team of FC Barcelona, he rose to the Segunda División in his first season. He was his team's top scorer with 18 goals. In the 2010/11 season he was top scorer in the league with 32 goals in 36 games. On 19 January 2012, Soriano signed a contract until June 2015 with FC Red Bull Salzburg. He scored his first goal for RB Salzburg in a 2-1 home win over SC Wiener Neustadt. In the 2012/13 season under new coach Roger Schmidt he scored 26 goals in 33 Bundesliga games and gave 7 assists. In the 2013/14 season he recorded 31 goals and 17 assists in 28 games. He was top scorer in the Bundesliga. After 2012, he also won the double again with FC Red Bull Salzburg. After the end of the Europa League season, he was the top scorer in this competition with his eight goals. 2014/15 he was again top scorer of the Bundesliga. In the following championship season 2015/16, he won the cup and the championship with the team for the third time in a row. Soriano was again top scorer in both competitions. On 27 February 2017 he went to Beijing Guoan in China. In two years in China, he made 31 appearances in the Chinese Super League, scoring 25 goals. After the end of his contract he moved to al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia in January 2019. In August 2019 he returned to Spain and joined second division club FC Girona. On 24 September 2021 he ended his active career. Soriano went through all Spanish youth national teams up to the U-21. In December 2012 he was called up to the Catalan football team for the friendly against Nigeria on 2 January 2013. Jonathas Cristian de Jesus (born 6 March 1989), simply known as Jonathas, is a Brazilian footballer. He plays for Spanish club Elche CF as a forward. In his career, he played top-flight football in his own country, the Netherlands, Italy, Spain, Russia and Germany. He recorded figures of 61 games and 21 goals in La Liga for Elche and Real Sociedad, and three goals in 29 Serie A matches for Brescia, Pescara and Torino. On 31 January 2020, Jonathas returned to his former club Elche, now in Segunda División. Weeks later, he tested positive for COVID-19 on 15 March, during the 2020 coronavirus pandemic.

Jonckheere was a Belgian motor coach and bus builder. It was founded in 1881 by Henri Jonckheere in Roeselare. In 1881, Henri Jonckheere started building horse-drawn carriages in the village of Beveren, near Roeselare, West Flanders, Belgium. In 1902 Henri Jonckheere made his first luxury automobile. In 1922, Henri's son, Joseph Jonckheere, made his first body of a bus. In the 1930s, Jonckheere stopped making automobiles and only made bus and motor coach bodies. In 1994, Berkhof Groep purchased Jonckheere. In 1997, the company changed its name from Berkhof Groep to Berkhof Jonckheere Groep In 1998 it was bought by the VDL Groep, It changed its name from Berkhof Jonckheere Groep to VDL Jonckheere. In 2010, VDL Jonckheere, VDL Bova and VDL Berkhof were merged into one company called VDL Bus & Coach.
Jonny Kennedy (born 16 February 1990) is an English rugby union player for Sale Sharks in the Guinness Premiership. He was born in Leighton, Cheshire. He plays as a centre or on the wing.

Jong Tae-Se (born 2 March 1984), also known as Chong Taese, is a North Korean professional athlete. He is best known as an association football player. He was a member of the North Korean national team.

Jonathan Peter Wilkinson OBE (born 25 May 1979) is an English rugby union player who now plays in France for Toulon. He was born at Frimley Park Hospital in Frimley, Surrey, He was grew up in Farnham He played for England when the team won the 2003 Rugby World Cup. He was awarded the MBE in 2003 and then the OBE in 2004.

Erling Martin Jonny Nilsson (9 February 1943 – 22 June 2022) was a Swedish competitive speed skater. He won a gold medal at the 1964 Summer Olympics. Nilsson died on 22 June 2022 at the age of 79.

Jonathan Marc Bairstow, also known as Jonny Bairstow, is an English cricketer. He was born on September 26, 1989 in Bradford, West Yorkshire. He currently plays for the England cricket team and has played for Yorkshire County Cricket Club since 2009. Jonathan has also played in the Indian Premier League (IPL) for Sunrisers Hyderabad, Punjab King, and Mumbai Indians. Jonathan is known as a right hand wicket-keeper-batter. Jonny Bairstow was born on September 26, 1989 in Bradford, West Yorkshire. His father, David Bairstow, was also an English cricketer. He played for Yorkshire and England as a wicket-keeper. David died in 1998 when Jonny was eight years old from hanging after suffering from depression. David had taught Jonny how to play cricket and has remained a lasting inspiration. Jonny's chosen squad number, 51, is a tribute to his father's birth year. Jonny has a sister, Rebecca, and a half-brother, Andrew. Andrew is a former English cricketer and played for Derbyshire.

Jonny Greenwood (born 5 November 1972) is an English musician and composer. He plays guitar and writes music. He is best known as the lead guitarist and keyboard player of the rock band Radiohead. Greenwood is also a film composer. He has written music for movies such as There Will Be Blood, Phantom Thread, and The Power of the Dog. In 2003, the magazine Rolling Stone placed Greenwood and his bandmate Ed O'Brien at number 60 on its list of the "100 Greatest Guitarists of All Time". Greenwood was born in Oxford, England. He started playing music when he was a child. He learned to play the recorder, then the viola, and later the guitar. He studied music at Oxford Brookes University but left before finishing to work full-time with Radiohead. Jonny joined the band in 1991 with his older brother Colin Greenwood. The other members are Thom Yorke, Ed O'Brien, and Phil Selway. At first, Greenwood played keyboards and harmonica. He later became the lead guitarist. He is known for his experimental guitar playing. He uses electronic instruments and effects. Greenwood also plays keyboards, viola, ondes Martenot, and other instruments. Some of Radiohead's most famous albums include OK Computer (1997), Kid A (2000), and In Rainbows (2007). Greenwood started writing music for films in the 2000s. He has worked with director Paul Thomas Anderson on several movies. His music mixes classical instruments with modern sounds. He has been nominated for the Academy Award (Oscar) for Best Original Score four times. Greenwood is married to Israeli visual artist Sharona Katan. They have three children. He lives in Italy.

Jonathan Brodzinski (born June 19, 1993) is an American professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Los Angeles Kings, San Jose Sharks, and New York Rangers. Before playing in the NHL, Brodzinski played two seasons with the Fargo Force of the United States Hockey League (USHL), as well as, three years with the St. Cloud State Huskies of the Western Collegiate Hockey Association (WCHA) and National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He had a successful time with his teams. He was named to the NCHC All-Conference First Team. He was drafted 148th overall by the Los Angeles Kings of the 2013 NHL entry draft. On April 2, 2015, Brodzinski signed a two-year entry-level contract to join the Kings. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Ontario Reign. On March 25, 2017, the Kings called him up and Brodzinski made his NHL debut in a 3–0 loss against the New York Rangers. On April 4, he recorded his first two NHL points after assisting on goals by Nick Shore and Nic Dowd in a 6–4 win against the Edmonton Oilers. On July 14, Brodzinski signed a two-year, $1.3 million contract to stay with the Rangers. On November 18, Brodzinski scored his first NHL goal against James Reimer in a 4–0 win against the Florida Panthers. On July 2, 2019, Brodzinski signed a one-year contract to join the San Jose Sharks. He recorded one assist in three regular season games. On October 9, 2020, Brodzinski signed a one-year contract to join the New York Rangers. On February 28, 2022, Brodzinski signed a one-year contract to stay with the Rangers. On February 21, 2024, Brodzinski signed a two-year contract to stay with the Rangers. On July 1, 2026, Brodzinski signed a one-year contract to join the Washington Capitals.

Joost van der Westhuizen (20 February 1971 – 6 February 2017) was a South African former rugby union player. He played as a scrum-half for the national team. He played in the 1995 and 1999 Rugby World Cups. On 12 May 2011, van der Westhuizen's publicist announced that he had a muscle-related neural disease. It was believed to be a form of motor neurone disease. Doctors at the Cleveland Clinic in the United States have since confirmed that he had motor neurone disease. They believed he had only a 20% chance of living for two to five years. On 6 February 2017, van der Westhuizen died at a hospital in Johannesburg, South Africa from complications of motor neurone disease, aged 45.

Joonas Donskoi (born 13 April 1992) is a Finnish professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Seattle Kraken of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the San Jose Sharks and Colorado Avalanche.

Jord van Weeren (born 1994) is a Dutch bowler and bowling coach from Leiden. He represents the Netherlands at international competitions since 2008. He became 2022 European team champion. Van Weeren started with playing football when he was a child. In the same period he went often to the bowling hall because his mother played bowling. His model sister also played bowling on a high level. As a junior he competed as an exceptional case at a senior competition, and won. The junior head coach who was present advised him to started playing more competitions. Van Weeren competes at around seven international tournaments per year. He participated at the 2018 WTBA World Tenpin Bowling Championships. In 2019 he became twice national champion (Singles and Doubles). He became in European team champion in Helsinki in 2022, together with Michell Stinissen, Nick de Gelder, Mike Bergmann and Kenneth Ramos. As an amateur bowler he has to pay all the costs for the tournaments, training facilities and bowling balls. Van Weeren is bowling coach of the Dutch national team (under-18). In 2022 he was selected to become Leiden sport coach of the year. Van Weeren has an IT job at Rabobank. He uses all his holiday days for playing bowling tournaments.

Johannes “Joop” Fernhout (27 June 1920 - 9 October 1995) was a Dutch chess player and chess composer. During World War II, Fernhout worked at Statistics Netherlands. He was also a resistance member during the war. Fernhout became Master of Law in 1945 and moved for work to the Dutch Indies. During his business career there he was among others president of AVROS, an agricultural producers organization with 250,000 employees in North Sumatra. Fernhout became in 1948 chess champion of Batavia and West Java. Fernhout moved back to the Netherlands in 1958, where he was among others chairman of the Kamer van Koophandel (the Dutch Chamber of Commerce) in The Hague.

Joosje Burg (born 29 July 1997) is a Dutch field hockey forward from Veghel. She plays with HC 's-Hertogenbosch and the Netherlands women's national field hockey team. Burg plays with HC Den Bosch since 2015. Burg played with the national Under–21 team at the 2016 Women's Hockey Junior World Cup in Santiago, Chile. Burg was a reserve player during the 2020–21 Women's FIH Pro League and made her debut in the 2021–22 Women's FIH Pro League. She scored during the league several times. She was selected in the Netherlands squad for the 2022 Women's FIH Hockey World Cup, held in July 2022. The father of Burg died in January 2019 from a fatal accident during a holiday in Thailand.

Joona Koppanen (born 25 February 1998) is a Finnish professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Luleå HF of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He has also played for the Boston Bruins and Pittsburgh Penguins of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Koppanen played for Ilves of the Liiga. Before playing in the NHL, Koppanen played one season with Ilves of the Liiga. He was drafted 135th overall by the Boston Bruins in the 2016 NHL entry draft. On 14 April 2017, Koppanen signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Bruins. He was sent down to play for their AHL and ECHL-affiliates Providence Bruins and Atlanta Gladiators. On 12 January 2023, the Bruins called him up and Koppanen made his NHL debut in a 3–0 loss against the Seattle Kraken. On 22 January, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Nick Foligno goal in a 4–0 win against the San Jose Sharks. On 1 July, Koppanen signed a two-year contract to join the Pittsburgh Penguins. On 18 March 2025, Koppanen scored his first NHL goal against Ilya Sorokin in a 4–2 loss against the New York Islanders.

Jordan Hendry (born February 23, 1984 in Nokomis, Saskatchewan) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman that currently plays for Straubing Tigers of the DEL. He played college ice hockey with the University of Alaska Fairbanks Nanooks. Hendry has played in the National Hockey League with the Chicago Blackhawks from four seasons and the Anaheim Ducks for 2 games. He has also played for HC Lugano of the National League A. Hendry won the Stanley Cup with the Chicago Blackhawks on June 9, 2010 which he took to his hometown of Nokomis.

Jordan Schroeder (born September 29, 1990 in Prior Lake, Minnesota) is an American professional ice hockey right winger who currently plays for the Minnesota Wild of the National Hockey League (NHL). Schroeder played for two seasons with the U.S. National Team Development Program before he joined the Minnesota Golden Gophers of the Western Collegiate Hockey Association (WCHA) for two seasons, being named WCHA Rookie of the Year in 2009. He has also played for the American national junior ice hockey team and played in three World Junior Championships, where he set a record for career points by an American. Thought of as one of the best junior players before the 2009 NHL Entry Draft, Schroeder was picked 22nd overall by the Vancouver Canucks. He played with the Canucks and the minor teams for the Canucks until 2014, when he joined the Wild.

Jordan Staal (born September 10, 1988) is a Canadian professional ice hockey player for the Carolina Hurricanes of the National Hockey League (NHL). He is regarded as one of the NHL's premier penalty-killers, both for his strong defensive skills, along with his scoring touch that makes him a threat for shorthanded goals. He has also played for the Pittsburgh Penguins for 6 seasons before he was traded to the Carolina Hurricanes during the 2012 NHL Entry Draft on June 22, 2012. Jordan Lucella Elizabeth Chiles (born April 15, 2001) is an American gymnast. Chiles was born in Tualatin, Oregon, on April 15, 2001. Her father is Black and her mother is Latina. She was named after American basketball player Michael Jordan. She has four siblings. She grew up in Vancouver, Washington. She later moved to Spring, Texas in 2019 to train with American gymnast Simone Biles. In 2021, Chiles’ mother was in federal prison for embezzlement. That same year, Chiles did gymnastics at the University of California, Los Angeles. In 2023, Chiles's aunt and grandfather died. On March 18, 2018, Chiles was in the Stuttgart World Cup. She was in third place. On April 8, 2018 Chiles competed at the Pacific Rim Championships. At the 2020 Summer Olympics, Chiles helped the United States win a silver medal. In August 2022, Chiles was in the National Championships. She was third place. In September 2023, Chiles competed at the 2023 Pan American Games. At the 2024 Summer Olympics, Chiles helped the United States win a gold medal.

Jordan Binnington (born July 11, 1993) is a Canadian professional ice hockey goaltender. He currently plays for the St. Louis Blues of the National Hockey League (NHL). Binnington is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Blues in 2019. He is also a one-time All-Star, being named one in 2020. Internationally, Binnington plays for Canada and won a silver medal with them in 2026. Before playing in the NHL, Binnington played four seasons with the Owen Sound Attack of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with his teams. He helped the Attack during the playoffs. They defeated the London Knights, Plymouth Whalers, and Windsor Spitfires before defeating the Mississauga St. Michael's Majors four games to three to win the J. Ross Robertson Cup. This earned them a spot in the Memorial Cup tournament where they went 1–2. He won the Hap Emms Memorial Trophy for being the most outstanding goaltender of the Memorial Cup tournament. He finished the 2012–13 season with a 2.17 goals against average and a.932 save percentage in the regular season. He won the Dave Pinkney Trophy for being on the team with the lowest goals against average and was also named the OHL Goaltender of the Year. He was drafted 88th overall by the St. Louis Blues in the 2011 NHL entry draft. On May 29, 2012, Binnington signed a three-year, $1.95 million entry-level contract to join the Blues. He was sent down to play for their AHL and ECHL-affiliates Peoria Rivermen, Kalamazoo Wings, and Chicago Wolves. On January 14, 2016, the Blues called him up and Binnington made his NHL debut coming in for relief of Brian Elliott and stopping 2 of 3 shots in a 4–1 loss against the Carolina Hurricanes. On January 19, 2023, he stopped all 25 shots he faced to earn both his first NHL career win and shutout in a 3–0 win against the Philadelphia Flyers. On July 15, 2016, Binnington signed a one-year, $600,000 contract to stay with the Blues. On July 21, 2017, Binnington signed a one-year, $660,000 contract to stay with the Blues. On July 6, 2018, Binnington signed a one-year contract to stay with the Blues. He helped the Blues when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Winnipeg Jets, Dallas Stars, and San Jose Sharks. They went on to defeat the Boston Bruins four games to three in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Blues franchise history. On July 13, 2019, Binnington signed a two-year, $8.8 million contract to stay with the Blues. Binnington is married to Canadian actress Cristine Prosperi and they have one son together.

Jordan Kyrou (born May 5, 1998) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Washington Capitals of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the St. Louis Blues. Kyrou is a one-time All-Star, being named one in 2022. Before playing in the NHL, Kyrou played four seasons with the Sarnia Sting of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with the Sting. He won the Jim Mahon Memorial Trophy for being the OHL's top scoring right winger and was named to the OHL First All-Star Team. He was drafted 35th overall by the St. Louis Blues in the 2016 NHL entry draft. On July 27, 2016, Kyrou signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Blues. He was sent down to play with the AHL-affiliates Chicago Wolves and San Antonio Rampage. On October 4, 2018, the Blues called him up and Kyrou made his NHL debut in a 5–1 loss against the Winnipeg Jets. On October 11, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Alexander Steen goal in a 5–3 win against the Calgary Flames. On December 9, Kyrou scored his first NHL goal against Jacob Markström in a 6–1 loss against the Vancouver Canucks. On August 3, 2021, Kyrou signed a two-year, $5.6 million to stay with the Blues. On September 13, 2022, Kyrou signed a eight-year, $65 million contract to stay with the Blues. On June 23, 2026, the Blues traded Kyrou to the Washington Capitals in exchange for Milton Gastrin, Connor McMichael, and a 2026 first-round draft pick. Kyrou's younger brother Christian Kyrou is also a professional ice hockey player.

Jordan Oesterle (born June 25, 1992) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Milwaukee Admirals of the American Hockey League (AHL). He has also played for the Edmonton Oilers, Chicago Blackhawks, Arizona Coyotes, Detroit Red Wings, Calgary Flames, and Boston Bruins. Before playing in the NHL, Oesterle played parts of one season with the Sioux Falls Stampede of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and three years with the Western Michigan Broncos of the Central Collegiate Hockey Association (CCHA) and National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NHCH). He was not drafted by an NHL team. On March 31, 2014, Oesterle signed a two-year, $1.535 million entry-level contract to join the Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Oklahoma City Barons. On February 21, 2015, the Oilers called him up and Oesterle made his NHL debut in a 2–1 loss against the Anaheim Ducks. On March 3, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Luke Gazdic goal in a 5–2 loss against the Los Angeles Kings. On June 20, 2016, Oesterle signed a one-year, $585,000 contract to stay with the Oilers. On July 1, 2017, Oesterle signed a two-year, $1.3 million contract to join the Chicago Blackhawks. He played 55 regular season games with the Blackhawks. On December 29, Oesterle scored his first NHL goal against Cam Talbot in a 4–3 overtime win against his former team, the Edmonton Oilers. On July 12, 2018, the Blackhawks traded Oesterle along with Vinnie Hinostroza, Marián Hossa, and a 2019 third-round draft pick to the Arizona Coyotes in exchange for Andrew Campbell, MacKenzie Entwistle, Marcus Krüger, Jordan Maletta, and a 2019 fifth-round draft pick. He played parts of three seasons with the Coyotes. On July 28, 2021, Oesterle signed a two-year, $2.7 million contract to join the Detroit Red Wings. He then moved to Ripensia Timişoara and the Romania national football team for the 1934 World Cup in Italy. His team were beaten in the first round by eventual finalists, Czechoslovakia. He later coached Austrian side SC Helfort, then Beogradski SK in Yugoslavia in 1935. He then moved to Switzerland to coach FC Biel from 1936 to 1937, and FC Lucerne until 1938. He then trained German side Schwarz-Weiß Essen between 1938 and 1941, and VfL Altenbögge between 1941 and 1943. After the Second World War, he returned to coaching Schwarz-Weiß Essen from 1949 to 1951. He went on to train his former club, Rapid Vienna, for one season from 1953 to 1954. In this year they beat the London club Arsenal 6-1 on 25 May 1953. Uridil was also a businessman. He created his own brand of beer, Uridil, and a brand of sugar, Kracheln. The famous Viennese writer Hermann Leopoldi wrote a musical piece named Heute spielt der Uridil ("Today, Uridil is playing") in 1922. Pepi Uridil played a number of film roles, such as Pflicht und Ehre ("Necessity and Honour") in 1924. Josef Milnarik (2 August 1903 – 30 November 1969) was an Austrian footballer. He played for Wiener Amateur SV and in one match for the Austria national football team in 1924.

Josef Smistik (28 November 1905 – 28 November 1985) was an Austrian football player and manager. He played mainly for SK Rapid Wien. He was captain of the Austrian Wunderteam. He started at ESV Stadlau. In 1926 he moved to SK Rapid Wien. In his first season, Pepi Smistik was able to win the ÖFB Cup and reach the final of the Mitropapokal, the forerunner of the European Cup. 1937 the Rapid captain also left his club, and went back back to his youth club FC Stadlau. After that he played for Kremser SC as a player-coach. Scores and results list Austria's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Smistik goal. After the Second World War he was only coach. He managed the Swiss club FC Schaffhausen (1952-1955) in the top division. In the 1958/59 season he looked after Wiener Austria as section manager. Towards the end of his life he suffered from Parkinson's disease. On his 80th birthday he died after a stroke in the Lainz hospital. Josef Epp (1 March 1920 – 28 February 1989) was an Austrian footballer and manager. He played at the 1948 Summer Olympic Games with the Austrian national football team. He played in the forward position. Epp played mainly for Wiener Sport-Club and LASK. At the beginning of his sporting career, Epp was also an athlete with the Vienna Cricket and Football Club before deciding to play football. He started with SC Metallum Wien and went to Wiener Sport-Club in 1937. In his first full season in the top division, he was runner-up with the Sport-Club in 1937–38 and was also able to take second place in the scorer list behind Franz Binder with 15 goals. Even after the annexation of Austria by Germany, Epp continued to be one of the most successful strikers in the league and was third in the top scorers list twice in a row in 1939 and 1940. At the end of the war, Epp was in Upper Austria. He played for SV Libertas Bad Hall. In early 1946, he went back to Sport-Club. In the spring of 1946, Epp was the subject of a controversy in the daily newspapers about his status as a National Socialist. The player had already worked for the National Socialist secondary school students before the Anschluss and became a Hitler Youth functionary in 1938. The player was briefly banned in February and March 1946. Then the Vienna Football Association decided that Epp was not required to be registered and allowed to play. In the years that followed, Epp was regularly his club's top scorer, and in 1949, he was second in the top scorer list behind Erich Habitzl. At the end of 1950, he moved on to LASK, who had just been promoted to the top flight. After a year, Epp returned to Vienna. He played two more seasons for Vienna. In 1953, he moved to the Swiss first division club Servette Geneva. After his return, he took over the position of player-coach at SV Stickstoff Linz. Epp accepted an offer from LASK and reached the championship title with them in his last season as an active player in 1958. With 195 championship goals Epp is still one of the most successful goal scorers in Austria's top division. Epp received his first call-up in August 1937 when he won 6-3 with the amateur national team against Hungary and scored a goal. After the annexation of Austria, Epp was used several times in the Vienna city team. His first game for the Austrian national team followed against Hungary in a 3-2 winin Vienna on 14 April 1946. His last match was on 3 October 1948 in a 2-1 loss also versus Hungary. He played eight matches and scored five goals. Josef Haist (31 December 1894 – 21 January 1950) was an Austrian football player and coach. He played for Vienna AF from 1912 to 1919. He also played for the Austrian national team. He worked as a trainer for various clubs. At the age of 15 he joined Normannia. From there he went to Neptune. At the age of 17 he became a player for Wiener AF. After two years he suffered a broken leg, which forced him to take a long break. Then came the First World War. Between 1914 and 1917 he played five times for the Austrian national team, when he was back from the Russian front. Another broken leg in 1917 saw the end of his time as a player. He began his time as a coach at WAF. He led them to the Austrian Cup win with a 2-1 final victory over the Wiener Amateur SV. After the decline of the WAF, he coached Sturm Graz. He was the first full-time coach in the club's history. Occasionally he also played for Sturm. In 1926–27 he took over at Brigittenauer AC, which he led to runners-up. From 1927 to 1930 he worked for SC Brühl in Switzerland. In February 1930 he took over the Grazer AK. At the same time he also trained the Grazer Hakoah. In January 1934 he followed Karl Kurz at FC Basel, where he remained until the middle of the year. After he coached the Slovakian club Trenčín, he took over a club in Eskilstuna in Sweden for two years. In January 1938 he went to the Swiss second division club FC Winterthur. In April 1941 he became coach of Admira Vienna. In July 1947 Haist was hired by the Styrian Football Association as an association coach. From 1939 on Haist also worked as a gymnastics and sports teacher at a high school in Vienna.

Josef Schediwy ( 7 December 1882 - 14 September 1915 in Tashkent) was an Austrian football player. He played for SK Rapid Wien and the Austrian national football team. With Rapid he won the first Austrian championship in 1911/12. Schediwy was one of the older players at this time and was rarely used. He still contributed three goals in three games in this season to help Rapid win their first championship title. Schediwy was able to defend the title with the team and played two games in the championship. In the 1913/14 season he played his matches for the Rapid and reached second place. He played his first match for the Austrian national football team on 11 October 1903 versus Hungary. His last match was on 1 June 1909 versus England. Scores and results list Austria's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Schediwy goal. On 14 September 1915, Josef Schediwy died as a Russian prisoner of war in Tashkent.

Josef Kaltenbrunner (22 January 1888 – August 1951) was an Austrian national football player. The goalkeeper played for SK Rapid Vienna and the Austrian national football team from 1907 to 1913. He also took part in the 1912 Olympic Games. Josef Kaltenbrunner began his career at Rapid. He played for the Austrian national team just a few months later. The background was that the major Viennese clubs had fallen out with the association, so they did not send any players to the international match against Hungary on 5 May 1907. The ÖFV therefore handed over the organization of the international match to the then small club Rapid, which now provided seven players of its own. This team was able to win 3-1. Because the club got into debt and lost its place Kaltenbrunner moved to Vienna in 1909. 1911 he returned to Rapid and won the Austrian champions twice in 1912 and 1913. Josef Kaltenbrunner was also in the national team squad at the 1912 Olympic Games in Stockholm as the second man behind Otto Noll. After being eliminated in the quarter-finals, he was used in the games against Italy (5:1), Norway (1:0) and Hungary (0:3). He played his last international match on 15 June 1913 against Italy. His career ended when he was called up as a soldier right at the beginning of the First World War.

Josef Jech (4 October 1886 – 19 November 1957) was an Austrian footballer. He played in two matches for the Austria national football team in 1908. In 1908 he played two matches for Austria. His first match was on 8 June 1908 versus England. His last match was on 1 November versus Hungary.

Josef Taurer (16 November 1883 -1 August 1956) was an Austrian football player from the early days of the sport. He scored the first goal in the Austrian national team's first unofficial game against Switzerland in 1901 and the first goal in the first official game against Hungary in 1902. He played as Forward mainly for Wiener AC. Josef Taurer began his career as a football player in 1897 for “Jugendhort”. The team included future national players Josef Fischer, Gustav Huber and Johann Studnicka. 1897 Jugendhorst joined WAC. With the WAC he won all three ÖFU championships for the Tagblatt Cup. The striker stayed with WAC until 1908. After one season with the Vienna Cricket and Football-Club. After his active time he was active as a football referee. In 1922 he became deputy head of the WAC's football section. In Austria's first unofficial international match against Switzerland on 8 April 1901 he played as a left winger and scored the first international goal in a 4-0 win. In Austria's first official on 12 October 1902 he scored again the first goal in a 5-0 win versus Hungary. His last match was on 9 April 1905 in a 0-0 again versus Hungary. Scores and results list Austria's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Taurer goal. 6 matches and 2 goals for the Austrian national football team:1901-1905

Josef Haas (3 August 1937 – 18 January 2024) was a Swiss cross-country skier. He competed in the late 1960s. He won the 50 km bronze at the 1968 Winter Olympics in Grenoble. Haas was the first Swiss to earn a cross-country skiing Olympic medal. Haas died on 18 January 2024 at the age of 86.

Josef Herschl (16 June 1897 - 13 July 1960) was an Austrian footballer. He played in the 1910s as goalkeeper. Hersch played for VfB Mödling, Fünfhaus and SK Rapid Wien as goalkeeper. In the 1915-1916 season he became Austrian champion with SK Rapid Wien.

Josef Hagler (1 February 1893 - 1 August 1972) was an Austrian football player. He played as midfielder for SK Rapid Wien. In 1912 he played one match for the Austrian national football team. He played his only game for the Austrian national football team on 3 November 1912 versus Hungary. 4 x Austrian champion (1911/12, 1912/13, 1915/16, 1916/17)

Josef Jelínek (9 January 1941 – 29 November 2024) was a Czech footballer. He played as a forward. He made 10 appearances for the Czechoslovakia national team, scoring twice from 1961 to 1962. He was born in Prague, Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia. Jelínek died on 29 November 2024 in Prague, Czech Republic at the age of 83.

Josef Karl Frühwirth (29 May 1907 in Vienna – 18 January 1944 near Kalikhovo, Soviet Union ) was an Austrian football player. With SK Rapid the midfielder became Austrian Champion twice. He also played one match for the Austrian national football team. Josef Frühwirth played his first championship match for SK Rapid Wien in the 1927-28 season. In the following season he made regular appearances in the first team and was able to win the championship title with Rapid. In the following season, Hütteldorf won the championship again, but Frühwirth was unable to secure a regular place. He left the club at the end of the season. He joined SC Wacker Wien. In 1932 he moved to the newly promoted FC Libertas Wien. With this team he played in the top division for four years. In 1936 he accepted a contract with SK Sturm Graz. He then worked as a player-coach at CA Spora Luxembourg and won the national championship in 1938. After his return to Austria he played for Floridsdorfer AC and again for Sturm Graz. On 7 October 1928, he made his only appearance for the national team in the 5:1 victory against Hungary. He was killed in early 1944 on the Eastern Front in Kalikhovo in what is now Russia.

Josef Hamerl (* 22 January 1931 in Vienna - 15 July 2017 ) was an Austrian football player. The forward played for Wiener Sport-Club and other teams in Austria. He also played for the Austrian national football team. Josef Hamerl began his football career after the end of the Second World War with the small clubs ASK Erlaa and SC Siebenhirten. Then he joinined FC Wien in early 1952. He made his league debut in a 2-0 home win against Floridsdorfer AC in the 22nd round, where he immediately shot his first goal. He soon became a regular player. Soon he attracted the interest of several top Austrian clubs. In the spring of 1955he moved to Austria Wien. Because he spent most of the time on the bench he returned after six months to FC Wien. 1956 he moved to Wiener Sport-Club. Together with Walter Horak, Adolf Knoll, Erich Hof and Karl Skerlan, he formed the famous Sport-Club strike force. He and his team remained undefeated for two years (41 matches). Perhaps his most famous performance was in the European Cup. He scored four goals in the legendary 7-0 victory over Italian champions Juventus Turin. In 1961 Hamerl, along with fellow striker Karl Skerlan, moved to Admira Vienna. After only two years with Admira, he returned to Sport-Club. There he was unable to repeat his successful years. Hamerl played his last season in the Austrian league in 1967 for 1. Wiener Neustädter SC. The year before he played for Kapfenberger SV. He scored 158 goals in Austria's top division. His first match for the Austrian national football team was on 23 March 1958 in a 3-2 win over Italy. His last match was a 1-0 loss versus Egypt on 5 January 1962. He played 9 matches and scored 2 goals. Josef Černý (18 October 1939 – 24 July 2025) was a Czech professional ice hockey player. He played in the Czechoslovak Extraliga. He won a three medals at four Winter Olympics while playing for the Czechoslovakia men's national ice hockey team. He was honored into the IIHF Hall of Fame in 2007. His career lasted from 1957 until 1979. Černý was born in Rožmitál pod Třemšínem, then-Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia. Černý died on 24 July 2025, at the age of 85.

Josef Mirschitzka (* 13 January 1914 in Vienna; † 25 May 1980 in Vienna) was an Austrian football player. He played mainly for SK Admira Wien. Mirschitzka played for SK Admira Wien in the first league championship organized by the Vienna Football Association. During this time he won the championship twice with the team as a defender. He won the ÖFB Cup in 1932 against Wiener AC (6:1; on May 26th) and in 1934 against SK Rapid Wien (8:0; on May 10th). In the 1938-39 season after the occupation by Germany he played in the Gauliga Ostmark. Admira became champion this season and played in the German championship. In the competition, which was held in four groups, his team came first in Group 3. In this he played the third and sixth game, scoring his only goal in the 8-3 win over VfR Mannheim in Vienna, with the goal to make it 1-0 in the second minute. The final with FC Schalke 04 on June 18, 1939 in the Berlin Olympic Stadium ended with a clear 0-9 defeat for him and his team. Josef Mirschitzka died in 1980. Josef Klima was an German footballer. He played at the beginning of the 20th century as midfielder for SK Rapid Wien In 1911 he moved from Wacker München to SK Rapid Wien.
Josefa Benitez Guzman (born August 30, 1969 in Barcelona) is a cyclist from Spain. She has a physical disability. She competed at the 2012 Summer Paralympics. She finished second in the road race.

Josef Šural (30 May 1990 – 29 April 2019) was a Czech footballer. He played as a forward. Šural was born in Hustopeče. He played for Czech sides Brno, Slovan Liberec and Sparta Praha. At the time of his death, he was playing for Turkish club Alanyaspor since early 2019. He played for the Czech Republic from 2013 until his death in 2019. He played for his country 20 times, scoring once. He also played for the Czech Republic at the UEFA Euro 2016. On 29 April 2019, Šural team's minibus overturned near the Turkish coastal town of Alanya. Šural was taken to hospital where he died. Seven other players were injured.

Joseline Landeros Palacios (born 20 December 2000) is a Mexican volleyball player. She played at the 2019 FIVB U20 Women's World Championship and 2018 FIVB Women's World Championship. She played for Nuevo Leon.
Joseph-Désiré Job (born 1 December 1977) is a former professional footballer who played as a forward. Born in France, he played for the Cameroon national team.

Joseph Henry Blackburne (Manchester, 10 December 1841 – London, 1 September 1924), nicknamed 'The Black Death', was the leading British chess Grandmaster during the later part of the 19th century. Blackburne learned the game at the relatively late age of 18 but quickly became a strong player. He went on to develop a professional chess career that spanned over 50 years. At one point he was the world's second most successful player, with a string of tournament victories behind him. Blackburne especially enjoyed giving simultaneous and blindfold displays around the country. Blackburne also annotated a collection of his own games (explained the moves), and was a chess correspondent for a leading journal until his death. "For more than 20 years he was one of the first six players in the world, and for even longer the leading English-born player".p42 Blackburne was fond of Scotch whisky, and often drank during a display. He once drank his opponent's glass, and said: "He left it en prise, and I took it en passant!" Much loved, he was supported by subscriptions from his fans in his last years.

Joseph LaBate (born April 16, 1993) is an American professional ice hockey center. He currently plays for the Vancouver Canucks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Columbus Blue Jackets. Outside of the NHL, LaBate has played for Barys Astana of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, LaBate played four years with the Wisconsin Badgers of Big Ten Conference (B1G). He was drafted 101st overall by the Vancouver Canucks in the 2011 NHL entry draft. On April 30, 2015, LaBate signed a two-year, $680,000 entry-level contract to join the Canucks. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Utica Comets. On November 23, 2016, the Canucks called him up and LaBate made his NHL debut in a 4–1 win against the Arizona Coyotes. After 13 games, he was sent back down to the Comets. He became a free agent after his contract ended. On August 20, 2018, LaBate signed a one-year contract to join the Belleville Senators of the American Hockey League (AHL). He played three seasons with the Senators. On July 29, 2021, he left the Senators and signed a one-year contract to play for the Milwaukee Admirals. On July 18, 2022, he left the Admirals and signed a one-year contract to play for the Chicago Wolves. On July 4, 2023, LaBate decided to head overseas and signed a one-year contract to play for Barys Astana of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). During his season with the team, he scored 8 goals and recorded 10 assists for 18 points. On November 29, 2024, LaBate signed a one-year, $775,000 to join the Columbus Blue Jackets. He played 6 regular season games with the Blue Jackets and spent most of his time with their AHL-affiliate Cleveland Monsters. On July 1, 2025, LaBate signed a one-year contract to rejoin the Vancouver Canucks. On February 27, 2025, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Sean Kuraly goal in a 4–1 win against the Arizona Coyotes.

Joseph Yobo (born 6 September 1980) is a Nigerian football player who plays for Everton in the Premier League. He is a defender who normally plays in the centre, but can play on the right of defence or in midfield. He signed from French side Olympique Marseille in 2001 and has become a favourite at Everton ever since. He is the Everton vice-captain and first captained Everton against Larissas in a 3-1 victory in the UEFA Cup, replacing the injured Phil Neville. Yobo is also captain of the national Nigerian side.
