Kevin Weekes (born April 4, 1975) is a Canadian studio analyst and former professional ice hockey goaltender. He played parts of 16 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Florida Panthers, Vancouver Canucks, New York Islanders, Tampa Bay Lightning, Carolina Hurricanes, New York Rangers, and New Jersey Devils. Since retiring, Weekes has become a studio analyst for both the NHL Network and Hockey Night in Canada. When he started the job in 2009, he became the first black analyst in ice hockey. Before playing in the NHL, Weekes played parts of two seasons with the Owen Sound Platers and one season with the Ottawa 67's of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 41st overall by the Florida Panthers in the 1993 NHL entry draft. He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Carolina Monarchs. On October 16, 1997, the Panthers called Weekes up and he made his NHL debut in a 4–0 loss against the Dallas Stars. He played 11 regular season games with the Panthers, ending with a 3.96 goals against average and a.870 save percentage. On January 18, 1999, the Panthers traded the right to Weekes along with Ed Jovanovski, Dave Gagner, Mike Brown, and a 2000 first-round draft pick to the Vancouver Canucks in exchange for Pavel Bure, Bret Hedican, the rights to Brad Ference, and a 2000 third-round draft pick. He played parts of two seasons with the Canucks. On December 19, 1999, the Canucks traded Weekes along with Bill Muckalt and Dave Scatchard to the New York Islanders in exchange for Felix Potvin, and both a 2000 second- and third-round draft pick. He played 36 regular season games with the Panthers, ending with a 3.41 goals against average and a.902 save percentage. On June 24, 2000, the Islanders traded Weekes along with the rights to Kristian Kudroc and a 2001 second-round draft pick to the Tampa Bay Lightning in exchange for a 2000 first-, fourth-, and seventh-round draft pick. On June 24, 2000, the Lightning traded Weekes to the Carolina Hurricanes in exchange for Chris Dingman and Shane Willis. On June 6, 2003, Weekes signed a one-year contract to stay with the Hurricanes. On August 26, 2004, Weekes signed a contract to join the New York Rangers. On August 2, 2005, Weekes signed a contract to stay with the Rangers. He played parts of two seasons with the Rangers. On August 26, 2004, Weekes signed a two-year, $1.375 million contract to join the New Jersey Devils. He played parts of two seasons with the Devils. On September 27, 2009, Weekes announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey.

Kevin Stenlund (born 20 September 1996) is a Swedish professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Utah Mammoth of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Columbus Blue Jackets, Winnipeg Jets, and Florida Panthers. Outside of the NHL, Stenlund has played for HV71 of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). Stenlund is a one-time Stanley Cup champion with the Panthers in 2024 and a one-time Le Mat Trophy champion with HV71 in 2016. Before playing in the NHL, Stenlund played three seasons with HV71 of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He had a successful time with HV71 and helped them during the playoffs. They defeated the Färjestad BK and Malmö Redhawks. They went on to defeat the Brynäs IF four games to three in the Final to win Le Mat Trophy. He was drafted 58th overall by the Columbus Blue Jackets in the 2015 NHL entry draft. On 23 May 2017, Stenlund signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Blue Jackets. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Cleveland Monsters. On 12 January 2019, the Blue Jackets called him up and Stenlund made his NHL debut in a 2–1 overtime win against the Washington Capitals. On 17 December, Stenlund scored his first NHL goal on the powerplay against Jonathan Bernier in a 5–3 win against the Detroit Red Wings. He played parts of four seasons with the Blue Jackets. On 13 July 2022, Stenlund signed a one-year contract to join the Winnipeg Jets. He scored 6 goals and recorded 3 assists in 54 regular season games with the Jets. On 1 July 2023, Stenlund signed a one-year, $1 million contract to join the Florida Panthers. He helped the Panthers during the playoffs. They defeated the Tampa Bay Lightning, Boston Bruins, and New York Rangers. They went on to defeat the Edmonton Oilers four games to three in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Panthers franchise history. On 1 July 2024, Stenlund signed a two-year, $4 million contract to join the Utah Hockey Club (later Utah Mammoth).

The Kia Granbird is a high-decker coach made by the South Korean automotive company Kia. It has been in production since 1994 and is used mainly for commercial and passenger transport. The Granbird is produced at Kia's Hanam plant. The first generation of the Kia Granbird was introduced in 1994. This model was developed to compete with other buses like the Hyundai Aero and Daewoo BH series. The first-generation Granbird came with diesel engines that used direct injection technology. The design of the first generation remained largely the same until the introduction of the second generation in 2007. The second generation of the Kia Granbird was launched in 2007 and featured a new model called the Parkway. This generation shared a commercial vehicle chassis with the Hyundai Universe. It received a refresh in 2011, and another update, known as the Silkroad model, was introduced in 2015 at the Seoul Motor Show. The third generation of the Kia Granbird was unveiled on May 14, 2020. It continued to use the commercial chassis shared with the Hyundai Universe. This generation included a large instrument cluster and touchscreen infotainment system. The interior had an increased indoor height and expanded width. It also introduced safety features such as a front parking assist system and automatic door sensors. The engine for the third generation is a Hyundai D6CG diesel engine with a capacity of 12.7 liters and a power output of 440 horsepower. This engine is available with both manual and automatic transmissions. The Kia Granbird is mainly available in South Korea, where it is used for long-distance travel and city routes. The bus is also sold in other countries in Asia and select international markets. It is often used by bus companies for public transportation and tour services.

On July 22, 2021, Sherwood signed a one-year contract to stay with the Avalanche. On July 14, 2022, Sherwood signed a two-year, $1.55 million contract to join the Nashville Predators. On April 16, 2023, Sherwood signed a one-Year, $775,000 contract to stay with the Predators. On July 1, 2024, Sherwood signed a two-year, $3 million contract to join the Vancouver Canucks. On December 16, Sherwood recorded his first NHL career hat-trick in a 3–1 win against the Colorado Avalanche. He played two seasons with the Canucks. On January 19, 2026, the Canucks traded Sherwood to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for Cole Clayton, a 2026 second-round draft pick, and a 2027 second-round draft pick. On March 4, 2026, Sherwood signed a five-year, $28.75 million contract to stay with the Sharks.

Kimberly Kay (born 20 September 1989) is a South African water polo player. She competed for the South Africa women's national water polo team in the 2011 World Aquatics Championships, 2013 World Aquatics Championships, and 2015 World Aquatics Championships.

Kimberly Exner (born 16 July 1977) is a Canadian volleyball player. She is part of the Canadian women's national volleyball team. She competed at the 2002 FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship. She played for Eastern Washington University's women's volleyball team.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli (; born 25 August 2006 in Bologna) is an Italian racing driver, who has been competing in the FIA Formula One World Championship for Mercedes AMG Petronas Formula One Team since 2025, currently 1st in the Drivers Championship with points, having taken his maiden win at the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix (with Mercedes). He is the son of racing driver Marco Antonelli. He replaced Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes in 2025 after the 7-time World Champion left for Scuderia Ferrari HP after 11 years with the Anglo-German team. Kimmie Meissner (born 4 October 1989) is a figure skater from the United States. She won the World Championships in 2006 and the United States national championships in 2007. She is the second American woman and the sixth woman worldwide to do a triple Axel jump. Meissner was a very good skater as a child. In 2003, she won the Novice title at the United States nationals. In 2004, she won the Junior title. In 2005, she won the bronze medal at the Senior level. While this would normally have given her a spot to the World Championships, Meissner was too young to go. In 2006, she went to the 2006 Olympics, where she placed 6th. At the Olympics, she was called the future of American skating. The future came quickly. The next month, she won the World Championships, placing ahead of the Olympic silver medalist Sasha Cohen. In 2007, Meissner won the United States championships and the Four Continents Figure Skating Championships, a competition for skaters from countries that are not in Europe. Meissner is a very popular skater, especially in Baltimore, where she is from. She has done shows in Baltimore and is a local celebrity. Meissner has many endorsements, which means she gets money from telling people she uses products. She is also involved with the Cool Kids, which is an organization to help kids with cancer.

Kimmo Samuel Timonen (born March 18, 1975) is a Finnish former professional ice hockey defenceman. He played a total of sixteen seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Nashville Predators, Philadelphia Flyers, and Chicago Blackhawks. He also played for KalPa, TPS, and HIFK of SM-liiga (SM-l), HC Lugano of National League A (NLA), and Brynäs IF of the Elitserien (SEL). Before playing in the NHL, Timonen played parts of 7 years in the SM-liiga with KalPa, TPS, and HIFK. He was drafted 250th overall by the Los Angeles Kings in the 1993 NHL Entry Draft. He continued to play in the SM-liiga after the draft. He helped Finland win the bronze medal at the 1998 Winter Olympics in Nagano. A little while after the Olympics, the Kings traded Timonen along with Jan Vopat to the Nashville Predators (who did not begin playing yet) in agreement that the Predators would not draft Garry Galley in the 1998 NHL Expansion Draft. Timonen would spend time between the Predators and their IHL affiliate, the Milwaukee Admirals. He was called up to the Predators during 1999-2000 season. He played the next four seasons with the Predators before the 2004–05 NHL lockout. He decided to travel back to Finland and play for KalPa during the lockout. On October 3, 2006, the Predators named Timonen the captain for the 2006–07 season. On June 18, 2007, the Predators traded Timonen along with Scott Hartnell to the Philadelphia Flyers in exchange for Philadelphia's first round pick (Jonathon Blum) in the 2007 NHL Entry Draft. After he signed, he became the highest paid Finn in the NHL after he signed a six-year, $37.8 million contract extension. Timonen and the Flyers faced the Washington Capitals in the first round of the playoffs. Philadelphia was able to win the series 4–3. In the second round of the playoffs, the Flyers played against the Montreal Canadiens and won the series 4–1. On April 30, 2008, Timonen was hit by a wrist shot at his foot by Canadiens defenseman Andrei Markov. He said that he had felt numbness in his foot but he didn't think it was anything but a twisted nerve. On May 8, 2008, a doctor at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania who looked at Timonen's foot said that he had found a small blood clot. This stopped Timonen from playing indefinitely and he missed the first four games of the Eastern Conference Finals against the rival Pittsburgh Penguins. He returned in game 5 but the Flyers lost and they were eliminated from the playoffs. On March 5, 2011, Timonen scored his 100th career goal against Ryan Miller of the Buffalo Sabres in a 5–3 loss. On August 5, 2014, Timonen was diagnosed with blood clots in his right leg and both of his lungs. He was ruled out from playing indefinitely and missed the first 62 games of the season. On February 27, 2015, the Flyers traded Timonen to the Chicago Blackhawks in exchange for a 2015 second-round pick and 2016 fourth-round pick. On 5 March, Timonen announced that he was going to retire from professional ice hockey at the end of the season. On 15 June, Timonen played his final game in the NHL. In his final game, he was able to help the Blackhawks defeat the Tampa Bay Lightning and win his first Stanley Cup. Captain Jonathan Toews celebrated with the cup and choose Timonen as the first player to hand it off to. During their visit to the White House, President Barack Obama congratulated Timonen and applauded him for his career and ability to play through his blood clots. Timonen would be inducted into the IIHF Hall of Fame in 2020.

Kimiko Shiratori is a former Japanese football player. She played for the Japan national team. Shiratori was born on June 6, 1968. In October 1984, when she was 16 years old, she was selected the Japan national team for tour for China. On October 17, she debuted for Japan against Italy. She played 5 games for Japan until 1986.

Christopher Alan "Chris" Pallies (November 7, 1955 – March 4, 2019) better known by his ring name, King Kong Bundy, was an American stand-up comedian, actor and professional wrestler. He was best known for wrestling with World Wrestling Federation. He won a Slammy Award in 1987 for the Bobby "The Brain" Heenan Scholarship Award. While he was signed to the WWF, Bundy had numerous feuds with Andre the Giant, Hulk Hogan and The Undertaker. Bundy died at his home in Glassboro, New Jersey on March 4, 2019, aged 63. Bundy held many championships during his professional wrestling career: AWA Superstars of Wrestling Heavyweight Championship (1 time) AWA Southern Heavyweight Championship (1 time) AWA Southern Tag Team Championship (1 time) - with Rick Rude NWA National Tag Team Championship (1 time) - with The Masked Superstar NWA New York Heavyweight Championship (1 time) NWA American Heavyweight Championship (2 times) NWA American Tag Team Championship (2 times) - with Bill Irwin (1) and Bugsy McGraw (1) Slammy Award for Bobby "The Brain" Heenan Scholarship Award (1987) with Haku, Tama, André The Giant, Hercules, and Harley Race

King Paul Akpan Udoh (born 5 September 1997) is an Italian footballer. He plays as a forward for Pianese. Udoh was born in Reggio Emilia and comes from a Nigerian background. He played youth football for Reggiana before signing for Juventus. He was loaned to many clubs while at Juventus, and signed for Viareggio 2014 in 2018. On 14 July 2019, he signed with Pianese. In February 2020, during the 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic, it was made clear that Udoh had tested positive to COVID-19.

Kingsley Junior Coman (born 13 June 1996) is a French professional footballer who plays as a winger for Bayern Munich and the France national team. Scores and results list France's goal tally first. Kingsley Ben-Adir (born 20 November 1986) is a British actor. He is known for playing Marcus Summer in ITV's Vera (2014–2018), Karim Washington on Netflix's The OA (2019), and Colonel Ben Younger in the BBC drama Peaky Blinders (2017–2019). In movies, he played Malcolm X in the Amazon Studios movie One Night in Miami... (2020), Basketball Ken in Barbie (2023) and Bob Marley in the biopic Bob Marley: One Love (2024).

Kinjiro Shimizu was a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. In May 1925, when Shimizu was a Kwansei Gakuin University student, he was selected the Japan national team for Far Eastern Championship Games in Manila. At this competition, on May 20, he debuted against Republic of China. But Japan lost in this match (0-2).

The Kinston Indians were a Minor league baseball team in Kinston, North Carolina. The team played in the Carolina League from (1956–1957, 1962–1974 and 1978–2011). Professional baseball in Kinston started in 1908, and there have been many teams since then. 2007 was the twenty-first season the Kinston team had been known as the Indians. Before that they were known as the Eagles and the Blue Jays. The Indians, or K-Tribe as they were nicknamed, played their home games in Grainger Stadium. The Indians' mascot was a dog named Scout. The Kinston Indians won their league championship in 1988, 1991, 1995, 2004 and 2006. For the 2012 season the Indians moved to Zebulon, North Carolina to become the Carolina Mudcats. The team still plays in the Carolina League. - Over the years, this publication has also been known as Carolina League Media Guide and Record Book and Carolina League Directory and Record Book

Simon James Kippen (born 19 May 1992) is an English professional wrestler. He currently wrestles for All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and their sister promotion Ring of Honor (ROH) under the ring name Kip Sabian. He is a member of the Patriarchy stable. Sabian has also wrestled in Ring of Honor (ROH) before it was bought by AEW. In February 2019, Sabian signed a contract with All Elite Wrestling (AEW). At Double or Nothing, Sabian made his AEW in-ring debut in a loss to Sammy Guevara. He also faced "Hangman" Adam Page at Fight for the Fallen but lost again. He began a feud with The Elite. He went on to face Kenny Omega on the December 10 episode of Dark and Cody on the January 29, 2020 episode of Dynamite but lost both times. Sabian announced that he and his real-life girlfriend Penelope Ford were going to get married and teased who his best man was going to be. The reveal was held on the 9 September episode of Dynamite and Miro was revealed as Sabian's best man. Sabian began teaming with Miro and they feuded with Best Friends. On the 28 April episode of Dynamite, the partnership between Sabian and Miro ended after Miro turned on and attacked him backstage. On the 24 August 2022 episode of Dynamite, Sabian made his return to AEW after injury and attacked Pac. At All Out: Zero Hour, Sabian challenged Pac for his AEW All-Atlantic Championship but lost. At AEW Battle of the Belts V, Sabian challenged Orange Cassidy for the All-Atlantic Championship but lost. After a confrontation at Blood & Guts, Sabian began a feud with Nick Wayne and The Patriarchy. Sabian eliminated Wayne during the Royal Rampage match. On the 23 October episode of Dynamite, Sabian turned heel and saved Christian Cage from being attacked by Hook. Sabian officially joined The Patriarchy two weeks later. Kippen is married to fellow professional wrestler and AEW employee Penelope Ford. They got legitimately married at Beach Break on 3 February 2021.

Kira Alekseyevna Zvorykina (September 29, 1919 – September 6, 2014) was a former Soviet-born Belarusian chess player who spent many years living in Belarus. Zvorykina was born in Mykolaiv, Ukraine. She was a three-time winner of the Women's Soviet Championship. Zvorykina died in Minsk, Belarus from natural causes, aged 94.

Kiran Bedi (born 9 June 1949) is a retired Indian Police Service officer, and former tennis player. She is the former Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry. She is the first female Indian Police Service (IPS) officer.

Kira Homeyer (born 1998) is a German athlete in wheel gymnastics. She has won 14 world champion titles. Homeyer comes from a family of gymnasts. Her parents, Jürgen Bientzle (brother of Wolfgang Bientzle) and Katja Homeyer, were both wheel gymnasts and coaches. Her brother Marvin and her sister Finia also do the sport. She started training very young. She performed in shows with her mother. When she was 15, she joined the German junior national team. She competed at her first World Championships in Chicago in 2013. She won gold in the all-around and vault. At the 2015 World Championships in Lignano, she won gold in all events. In 2015, at age 17, she switched early to the adult category. At the 2016 World Championships in Cincinnati, she won gold in straight line and team, and silver in all-around. At the 2018 World Championships in Magglingen, she won three gold medals (all-around, straight line, team), one silver (vault), and one bronze (spiral). She won two more world titles in all-around and straight line at the 2024 World Championships in Almere. She was honoured from her city.

Anthony Kirby Puckett (more often known simply as Kirby Puckett; March 14, 1960 - March 6, 2006) was an American baseball player. He was born in Chicago. He played for the Minnesota Twins from 1984 to 1995. He had many home run hits and doubles. He retired because of bad vision in one eye. Kirby died on March 6, 2006 in Phoenix, Arizona from a hemorrhagic stroke.

Kirby Dach (born January 21, 2001) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Montreal Canadiens of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Chicago Blackhawks. Before playing in the NHL, Dach played parts of three seasons with Saskatoon Blades of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with the Blades. He was named as an alternate captain for the team in January 2019 and played in that year's CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game where he captained Team Orr. He was drafted 3rd overall by the Chicago Blackhawks in the 2019 NHL entry draft. On July 8, 2019, Dach signed a three-year, entry-level contract to join the Blackhawks. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Rockford IceHogs. He played 3 games with them before being called up to the Blackhawks. On October 20, 2019, Dach made his NHL debut in a 5–3 loss against the Washington Capitals. On October 22, he scored his first NHL goal against Marc-André Fleury in a 2–1 loss against the Vegas Golden Knights. He helped the Blackhawks during the playoffs. They defeated the Edmonton Oilers three games to one in an upset victory, knocking them out of the playoffs. They were eventually defeated by the Vegas Golden Knights four games to one in the first round. He missed much of the next season after suffering a wrist injury during the 2021 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships. During the 2022 NHL entry draft on July 7, the Blackhawks traded Dach to the Montreal Canadiens in exchange for the 13th overall pick and a second-round pick. On September 7, 2022, Dach signed a four-year, $13.45 million contract to stay with the Canadiens. Dach's younger brother Colton is also a professional ice hockey player and plays for the Chicago Blackhawks.

Kirk James Hinrich (born January 2, 1981) is an American professional basketball player. He plays for the Chicago Bulls. Hinrich played for the Chicago Bulls from 2003 through 2010, then again since 2012. He played for the Washington Wizards from 2010 through 2011. He played for the Atlanta Hawks from 2011 through 2012. Hinrich was born on January 2, 1981 in Sioux City, Iowa.

Kirk Baptiste (June 20, 1962 – March 24, 2022) was an American track and field athlete. He mainly competed in the 200 metres. He was born in Beaumont, Texas. He competed for the United States at the 1984 Summer Olympics held in Los Angeles, United States, where he won the silver medal in the 200 metres with a time of 19.96 seconds. Baptiste was born in Beaumont, Texas. Baptiste was diagnosed with HIV in the 1990s. He died on March 24, 2022 at the age of 59.

Kiril "Kiro" Dojčinovski (Macedonian: Kиpил Kиpo Дojчинoвcки; 17 October 1943 – 10 August 2022) was a Macedonian footballer. He played for the Yugoslavia national football team from 1968 until 1970, making six appearances. Dojčinovski died on 10 August 2022 at the age of 78.

Kiril Lozanov Ivkov (; 21 June 1946 – 24 May 2025) was a Bulgarian footballer and manager. As a footballer,he mainly played as a defender for Minyor Pernik and Levski Sofia. With Levski Sofia, he scored 15 goals in 375 matches, and won four Bulgarian League titles, four Bulgarian Cups, and was named was named Bulgarian Footballer of the Year in 1974 and 1975. He was also capped 44 times for Bulgaria, and played for them at the 1968 Summer Olympics, where he won a silver medal, and at the 1974 FIFA World Cup. Ivkov died on 24 May 2025, at the age of 78. Bulgarian League: 1967–68, 1969–70, 1973–74, 1976–77 Bulgarian Cup: 1969–70, 1970–71, 1975–76, 1976–77 Silver Medal at the Summer Olympic Games: 1968 Bulgarian Footballer of the Year: 1974, 1975

Kirill Kudryavtsev (born 5 February 2004) is a Russian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Vancouver Canucks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Minnesota Wild. Outside of the NHL, Kudryavtsev played for Djurgårdens IF and Färjestad BK of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). Before playing in the NHL, Kudryavtsev played three seasons with the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 208th overall by the Vancouver Canucks in the 2022 NHL entry draft. On 10 March 2023, Kudryavtsev signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Canucks. They sent him down to play for their AHL-affiliate Abbotsford Canucks. On 14 April 2025, Vancouver called him up and Kudryavtsev made his NHL debut in a 2–1 overtime loss against the San Jose Sharks. On 12 April 2026, Kudryavtsev recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Curtis Douglas goal in a 4–3 overtime win against the Anaheim Ducks. He won the Calder Cup with the Abbotsford Canucks in 2025.

Kirill Olegovich Kaprizov (; born 26 April 1997) is a Russian professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Minnesota Wild of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Kaprizov played for Metallurg Novokuznetsk, Salavat Yulaev Ufa, and CSKA Moscow of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Kaprizov was the Calder Memorial Trophy winner in 2019. He is also a three-time All-Star, being named one in 2022, 2023, and 2024. Kaprizov is a one-time Gagarin Cup winner, winning with CSKA in 2019 and a five-time KHL All-Star. Internationally, Kaprizov plays for Russia. He won the gold medal with the Olympic Athletes from Russia in 2018. Before playing in the NHL, Kaprizov played two seasons with Metallurg Novokuznetsk, one season with Salavat Yulaev Ufa, and three seasons with the CSKA Moscow of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). During his time in the KHL, Kaprizov was named to five All-Star games. He also won the Golden Stick for being the league's most valuable player. Kaprizov won the Best Sniper Award back-to-back in 2019 and 2020. He helped the CSKA during the playoffs. They defeated the HC Vityaz, HC Dynamo Moscow, and SKA Saint Petersburg. They went on to sweep and defeat the Avangard Omsk in the Final to win the Gagarin Cup. He was drafted 135th overall by the Minnesota Wild in the 2015 NHL entry draft. On 13 July 2020, Kaprizov signed a two-year entry-level contract to join the Wild. On 14 January 2021, Kaprizov made his NHL debut in a 4–3 overtime win against the Los Angeles Kings. During the game, he recorded his first two NHL points after assisting on goals from Jonas Brodin and Victor Rask. He also scored his first NHL goal against Jonathan Quick which was the overtime winner. On 12 March, Kaprizov recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 4–0 win against the Arizona Coyotes. He finished his rookie season scoring 27 goals and recording 24 assists for 51 points in 55 regular season games. He was awarded the Calder Memorial Trophy as rookie of the year for his efforts and was the first player in Wild franchise history to win the trophy. He also set a Wild franchise record for both most goals and points by a rookie. On 21 September 2021, Kaprizov signed a five-year, $45 million contract to stay with the Wild and making him the league's highest-paid sophomore player. On 13 January 2022, he was selected to play in his first All-Star game. On 30 September 2025, Kaprizov signed a eight-year, $136 million contract to stay with the Wild. It was the richest contract in the league at the time of signing.

Kirill Igorevich Marchenko (; born 21 July 2000) is a Russian professional ice hockey winger. He currently plays for the Columbus Blue Jackets of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Marchenko played for HC Yugra and SKA Saint Petersburg of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, Marchenko played two regular season games with HC Yugra and parts of four seasons with SKA Saint Petersburg of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He was drafted 49th overall by the Columbus Blue Jackets in the 2018 NHL entry draft. On 2 May 2022, Marchenko signed a one-year entry-level contract to join the Blue Jackets. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Cleveland Monsters. On 6 December 2022, the Blue Jackets called him up and Marchenko made his NHL debut in a 4–1 loss against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On 11 December 2022, Marchenko scored his first NHL goal against Jonathan Quick in a 6–5 overtime win against the Los Angeles Kings. On 7 January 2023, Marchenko recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 4–3 shootout win against the Carolina Hurricanes. On 28 July 2024, Marchenko signed a three-year, $11.55 million contract to stay with the Jackets.

Kirk Alan McLean (born June 26, 1966) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey goaltender. He played parts of 16 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the New Jersey Devils, Vancouver Canucks, Carolina Hurricanes, Florida Panthers, and New York Rangers. McLean is a two-time All-Star, being named on in 1990 and 1992. Before playing in the NHL, McLean played parts of three seasons with the Oshawa Generals of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He also played 15 regular seasons games with the Nanaimo Clippers of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL). He was drafted 107th overall by the New Jersey Devils in the 1984 NHL entry draft. On April 5, 1986, McLean made his NHL debut in a 7–1 loss against the New York Islanders. On April 6, 1986, McLean stopped 20 of 27 shots in a 7–1 loss against the New York Islanders. After the two games, the Devils sent him down to play for their AHL-affiliate Maine Mariners. On September 15, 1987, the Devils traded McLean along with Greg Adams to the Vancouver Canucks in exchange for Patrik Sundström and a 1988 fourth-round draft pick. On February 17, 1988, McLean stopped all 27 shots he faced in a 5–0 win against the Pittsburgh Penguins to record his first NHL shutout. He started to find success during his time in Vancouver. Over the 1988–89 season, McLean posted a 20–17–3 record with a 3.08 goals against average and a.891 save percentage. For his efforts, the Canucks named him as their nominee for the Vezina Trophy and he finished third in voting. the next season, McLean was selected to play for in his first All-Star Game. On October 16, 1990, McLean signed a contract to stay with the Canucks. The next season, he was nominated for the Vezina Trophy again but it was won by Patrick Roy. He helped the Canucks when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Calgary Flames, Dallas Stars, and Toronto Maple Leafs. They were eventually defeated by the New York Rangers four games to three in the Final. He had some notable moments during the playoffs. During game 7 of the first round against the Calgary Flames. McLean scrambled back into position and stacked the pads to save an open net one-timer shot from Robert Reichel. He also posted back-to-back shutouts in game 3 and 4 against the Maple Leafs. On April 5, 1995, McLean signed a five-year, $2.4 million contract to stay with the Canucks. On January 2, 1998, the Canucks traded McLean along with Martin Gélinas to the Carolina Hurricanes in exchange for Sean Burke, Geoff Sanderson, and Enrico Ciccone. He played 8 regular season games with the Hurricanes. On March 23, the Hurricanes traded McLean to the Florida Panthers in exchange for Ray Sheppard. He played parts of two seasons with the Panthers. On July 13, 1999, McLean signed a two-year, $1.64 million contract to join the New York Rangers. He played parts of two seasons with the Rangers. McLean retired from playing professional ice hockey in 2001.

Kirsten Patricia Hudson (born 2 February 1988) is a New Zealand water polo player. She is a member of the New Zealand women's national water polo team. She played at the 2009 World Aquatics Championships, 2011 World Aquatics Championships, 2017 World Aquatics Championships, and 2018 FINA Women's Water Polo World Cup. She played for Hartwick College's women's water polo team.
Kirsten Andrea Fisher-Marsters is a swimmer from Cook Islands. Fisher-Marsters competed at the 2020 Summer Olympics. She was born on 11 February 1998.

Kirsty Leigh Coventry Seward (née Coventry; born 16 September 1983) is a Zimbabwean politician, sports administrator and former competitive swimmer. She has been the president of the International Olympic Committee since June 2025. She is the first woman, the first Zimbabwean, and the first African to hold that position. Coventry was a member of the Cabinet of Zimbabwe from September 2018 to March 2025 as the Minister of Youth, Sport, Arts and Recreation until September 2023. She was the Minister of Sport, Recreation, Arts and Culture before. She was an Olympic swimmer and world record holder. She is the most decorated African Olympian. At the 2004 Summer Olympics, in Athens, Coventry won three Olympic medals: a gold, a silver, and a bronze, and in the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing she won four medals: a gold and three silver. Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe called her "a golden girl". In 2016, Coventry retired from swimming after her fifth Olympics. Coventry was born in Harare on 16 September 1983 to Robert Edwin and Lyn Coventry. In 2000, while still in high school, Coventry qualified for the Olympics in Sydney. She became the first Zimbabwean swimmer to reach the semifinals at the Olympics and was named the country's Sports Woman of the Year. In August 2013, Coventry married Tyrone Seward, her swimming manager. In May 2019, she gave birth to their first child.

Kisho Yano is a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Yano was born in Hamamatsu on April 5, 1984. After graduating from Hamana High School, he joined J1 League club Kashiwa Reysol in 2003. He played as a substitute forward from first season. Although his opportunity to play increased later in the summer of 2005, Reysol was relegated to the J2 League at the end of 2005 season. In 2006, he was transferred to Albirex Niigata with teammate Mitsuru Nagata. He quickly established himself as a first-choice forward. Although his playing style was a tall center forward, he was converted to a right winger of three forwards in 2009 because Niigata acquired a similiar-style forward Hideo Oshima. In August 2010, Yano was transferred to German Bundesliga club Freiburg. After an unsuccessful stint in Europe, he returned to Japan and signed for Niigata in February 2012. Although he initially played as regular forward, he lost his position and he played many matches as a substitute forward from June. The club results were also sluggish and finished in the 15th place of 18 clubs in the 2012 season. In 2013, Yano moved to Nagoya Grampus. Although he initially played as the center forward instead of Joshua Kennedy who was injured, Kennedy came back in May and Yano played many matches as a substitute forward. In 2014, Yano was converted to right-back by new manager Akira Nishino and became a regular player as a right-back. Although he played as regular player every season, Nagoya finished at the 16th place of 18 clubs in 2016 season and was relegated to J2 League. In 2017, Yano re-joined Albirex Niigata for the first time in four years. Although he played many matches as a right-back, Niigata was relegated to J2 at the end of 2017 season. He returned to his original position by new manager Masakazu Suzuki in 2018. In 2020, he moved to Tochigi SC. On March 24, 2007, Yano debuted for the Japan national team against Peru. He was a member of the Japan team for the 2007 Asian Cup. He played two games as a substitute. In 2010. he was selected for the Japan team for 2010 World Cup. At the World Cup, he played one match as a substitute against Cameroon. This match was his last match for Japan. He played 19 games and scored 2 goals for Japan from 2007 to 2010. Scores and results list Japan's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Yano goal.

Kitanoumi Toshimitsu (北の湖敏満 Obata Toshimitsu; May 16, 1953 – November 20, 2015) was a Japanese sumo wrestler. He was the dominant yokozuna in sumo during the 1970s. Kitanoumi was promoted to yokozuna at age 21, becoming the youngest ever to achieve sumo's top rank, and he remained a yokozuna for a record 63 tournaments. He won 24 tournament championships during his career. Following his retirement in 1985 he established Kitanoumi stable. He was chairman of the Japan Sumo Association from 2002 until 2008, and from 2012 until his death. Kitanoumi died of multiple organ failure caused by colorectal cancer on the evening of November 20, 2015, aged 62. He was in Fukuoka for the Kyushu tournament and was taken to hospital for anemia in the morning, after which his condition deteriorated.

Christopher Robin Anthony "Kit" Napier (26 September 1943 – 31 March 2019) was a Scottish professional footballer. He played as a forward. He scored 119 goals from 379 appearances in the Football League. After graduating from Fujieda Higashi High School, he joined Yawata Steel (later Nippon Steel). In 1965, Yawata Steel joined new league Japan Soccer League. He retired in 1976, having played 164 games and scored 22 goals in the league. In October 1964, Tomizawa was selected the Japan national team for 1964 Summer Olympics in Tokyo. However, he did not play in the match. On March 14, 1965, he debuted for Japan against Hong Kong. In 1968, he was selected Japan for 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City. He played against Hungary in semifinal and Japan won Bronze Medal. In 2018, this team was selected Japan Football Hall of Fame. He also played at 1970 Asian Games. At 1972 Summer Olympics qualification in 1971, Japan's failure to qualify for 1972 Summer Olympics. This qualification was his last game for Japan. He played 9 games and scored 2 goals for Japan until 1965.

Kleomedes of Astypalia was an Ancient Greek boxer, who had a successful boxing career all throughout the 5th century BC. However, in either the 71st or 72nd Olympic Games (496 or 492 BCE), using an illegal strike, he killed his opponent Ikos. Because of this offense, and not due to the murder of his opponent, which was not considered a punishable act, he was disqualified and heavily fined by the judges. Kleomedes mourned his loss greatly, because it put a stain on his record, consequently, while returning to his home town Astypalia, in a flash of Mania, he pulled out the pillar supporting a school roof, purportedly killing at least 27 children. The people attempted to stoned him to death, but he fled into a temple and climbed into a holy chest. When the people opened it, he was gone. His confused persuers consulted the Oracle of Delphi, which told the people that Kleomedes had become a hero. From that moment onwards he was commemorated with annual sacrifices in his honour. His mythos is interpreted to comment on the nature of Rules. Translation 1 [6] At the Festival previous to this it is said that Cleomedes of Astypalaea killed Iccus of Epidaurus during a boxing-match. On being convicted by the umpires of foul play and being deprived of the prize he became mad through grief and returned to Astypalaea. Attacking a school there of about sixty children he pulled down the pillar which held up the roof. [7] This fell upon the children, and Cleomedes, pelted with stones by the citizens, took refuge in the sanctuary of Athena. He entered a chest standing in the sanctuary and drew down the lid. The Astypalaeans toiled in vain in their attempts to open the chest. At last, however, they broke open the boards of the chest, but found no Cleomedes, either alive or dead. So they sent envoys to Delphi to ask what had happened to Cleomedes. [8] The response given by the Pythian priestess was, they say, as follows:— “Last of heroes is Cleomedes of Astypalaea; Honor him with sacrifices as being no longer a mortal." So from this time have the Astypalaeans paid honors to Cleomedes as to a hero. Translation 2 “In the Olympiad before that one they say that Kleomêdês the Astupalaian killed the Epidaurian Hippos while boxing him. When he was charged by the referees with cheating and was deprived of the victory, he went out of his mind with grief and returned to Astupalaia. There, he attacked a school there which held as many as sixty children and knocked down the pillar which supported the roof. After the roof fell on the children, the citizens threw stones at Kleomêdês and he fled into the Temple of Athena. Inside, he climbed into a chest and closed the lid over him. The Astupalaians wore themselves out trying to open or break the chest. When they finally broke open the chest and did not find Kleomêdês there dead or alive, they send representatives to Delphi to ask what kind of thing had happened with Kleomêdês. The Pythia is said to have given the oracle that: "Kleomêdês the Astupalaian was the last of the heroes— Honor him with sacrifices since he is no longer mortal.” For this reason the Astupalaians have honored Kleomêdês as a hero since that time." Between different translations Kleomêdês kills either Ikos, Iccus or Hippos, but the story isn't ultimately changed by this.

Kobe Bean Bryant (; August 23, 1978 – January 26, 2020) was an American professional basketball player. He is considered one of the greatest basketball players of all time. Bryant is the youngest child of three children of his family. His father was also a basketball player and coach. Bryant played a career total of 20 years in the National Basketball Association. He played his entire career with the Los Angeles Lakers as a shooting guard. During the 2005–2006 season, he scored 81 points in a game against the Toronto Raptors. Bryant retired on April 13, 2016 after scoring 60 points in a Lakers win against the Utah Jazz. He won an Oscar and Emmy for his movie Dear Basketball. Kobe Bryant won five championship rings from 2000 to 2002, and again in 2009–2010. He was awarded the Most Valuable Player in the 2007-08 NBA season after the Los Angeles Lakers went to the 2008 NBA Playoffs as the first seed in the Western Conference was the winner of 18 times NBA all-star, 15-time member of the All-NBA team, 12-time member of the all-defensive team and 1-time slam dunk champion. In 2008, Bryant won a gold medal with the United States national team at the Olympics in Beijing. Bryant earned 14 selections for All-NBA teams and 12 for All-Defensive teams. He led the league in scoring twice. He received 4 all-star game MVPs in 14 appearances. He also won 2 finals MVP awards. He was also the youngest player to reach 30,000 points, passing Shaquille O Neal and Michael Jordan and becoming third on the all-time scoring list. Bryant is widely considered to be one of the greatest basketball players in NBA history. In the summer of 2003, the sheriff's office of Eagle, Colorado, arrested Bryant in connection with an investigation of a sexual assault complaint filed by a 19-year-old hotel employee. In September 2004, the assault case was dropped by prosecutors after the accuser refused to testify at the trial. On January 26, 2020, Bryant was killed in a helicopter crash in Calabasas, California that was intended to go to the Camarillo Airport, at the age of 41. His 13-year-old daughter, Gianna Bryant, and seven others also died in the crash. On February 24, a public funeral service was held at the Staple Center with Bryant's widow Vanessa and basketball legends such as Michael Jordan making speeches. In games after the crash, some teams took intention 24-second shot clock or 8-second backcourt violations to honor Bryant since both 24 and 8 were his jersey numbers. During the 2020 WNBA draft, Bryant's daughter Gianna, along with Alyssa Altobelli and Payton Chester were all made honorary draft picks. On February 8, 2024, a 19-foot bronze statue of Bryant was unveiled in the Star Plaza outside of Crypto.com Arena. On May 15, 2021, Bryant was posthumously inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame by his widow Vanessa.

Koichi Hashiratani is a former Japanese football player and manager. He played for the Japan national team. His brother Tetsuji Hashiratani also played for the Japan national team. Hashiratani was born in Kyoto on March 1, 1961. After graduating from Kokushikan University, he started his senior career with Japan Soccer League club Nissan Motors since 1983 and played with Nissan Motors for 9 seasons until transferred to Urawa Reds in 1992, right before J1 League's inauguration. He experienced another transfer to Kashiwa Reysol, then playing in Japan Football League in June 1994. Kashiwa was promoted to J1 League as of the end of 1994 season, and he also made his return to the top flight. He retired as a player end of 1996 season. In August 1979, when Hashiratani was a Kokushikan University student, he was selected the Japan U-20 national team for 1979 World Youth Championship. On February 8, 1981, he debuted for the Japan national team against Malaysia. In 1982, he was selected Japan for 1982 Asian Games. He also played at 1984 Summer Olympics qualification and 1986 World Cup qualification. In September 1986, he was selected Japan for 1986 Asian Games. This Game was his last game for Japan. He played 29 games and scored 3 goals for Japan until 1986. Hashiratani started his coaching career with Montedio Yamagata, where he managed for 3 years from 2001 to 2003. After 6 months of absence, he was named as a manager of Kyoto Purple Sanga in June 2004 when Kyoto was playing in J2 League, then contributed to Kyoto's promotion back to the top flight after the 2005 season. However, due to the poor performances and turnouts of the club, he was dismissed in October about 2 months before the end of 2006 season. He was named as a manager of Tochigi SC playing in Japan Football League in 2007. After two seasons, he made Tochigi eligible to be promoted to J2 League as the club finished 2nd in 2008 season, but was dismissed because he was unable to reach the consent with top managements about his pay, as well as recruiting of new players. He was named as a General Manager of Urawa Reds in December 2009, but was dismissed due to Urawa's poor performance in 2011 season. After spending one season as a commentator in 2012, he was named manager of Giravanz Kitakyushu and managed until 2016 season.

Koichi Oita was a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Oita was born in Tokyo Metropolis on April 9, 1914. In 1936, when he was a Tokyo Imperial University student, he was selected the Japan national team for 1936 Summer Olympics in Berlin. At this competition, on August 4, he debuted against Sweden. Although he was a midfielder, he played as a defender. Japan completed a come-from-behind victory against Sweden. The first victory in Olympics for the Japan and the historic victory over one of the powerhouses became later known as "Miracle of Berlin" (ベルリンの奇跡) in Japan. In 2016, this team was selected Japan Football Hall of Fame. On August 7, he also played against Italy. He played 2 games for Japan in 1936. After retirement, in 1947, Oita became a manager for new club Sumitomo Metal and managed until 1956. September 11, 1996, Oita died of heart failure in Bunkyo, Tokyo at the age of 82.

Koji Morisaki is a former Japanese football player. His twin brother Kazuyuki Morisaki, is also a former footballer. Morisaki was born in Hiroshima on May 9, 1981. He joined Sanfrecce Hiroshima from their youth team in 2000. He played many matches as an offensive midfielder from 2002 and became a central player of the club with his twin brother Kazuyuki Morisaki. In the 2000s, although he played many matches, he suffered from occupational burnout in 2005 and chronic fatigue syndrome in 2009. In the 2010s, although his opportunity to play decreased, the club won the champions 2012, 2013, and 2015 J1 League. He retired end of the 2016 season. In June 2001, Morisaki was selected for the Japan U-20 national team for the 2001 World Youth Championship. At this tournament, he played 2 matches. In August 2004, he was selected for the Japan U-23 national team for 2004 Summer Olympics. He played all 3 matches.

Koji Tanaka is a former Japanese football player and manager. He played for the Japan national team. Tanaka was born in Saitama on November 2, 1955. After graduating from Meiji University, he joined Japan Soccer League club Nippon Kokan (later NKK) in 1978. The club won the champions at 1980 JSL Cup and 1981 Emperor's Cup. From 1985, the club won the 2nd place for 3 years in a row in the league and won the champions 1987 JSL Cup. He retired in 1989. On July 15, 1982, Tanaka debuted for the Japan national team against Romania. In November, he played at 1982 Asian Games. In 1983 and 1984, he played at 1984 Summer Olympics qualification. He played 20 games and scored 3 goals for Japan until 1984. After retirement, Tanaka started coaching career at NKK in 1989. In 1993, he became a manager for the Japan U-20 national team. At 1995 World Youth Championship, he led U-20 Japan to advanced to the quarter-finals. In 1995, he signed with Nagoya Grampus Eight and became an assistant coach. In November 1997, he became a manager as Carlos Queiroz successor. He was sacked in April 1999. In 2001, he signed with J2 League club Shonan Bellmare and managed the club until 2002.

Koji Noguchi is a former Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Noguchi was born in Chiba Prefecture on June 5, 1970. After graduating from Funabashi Municipal High School, he joined Japan Soccer League club Fujita Industries (later Bellmare Hiratsuka) in 1989. Through Japan Football League (1992–93), the club was promoted to J1 League in 1994. The club were the winners of the 1994 Emperor's Cup. The club also won 1995 Asian Cup Winners' Cup. Although he played as a regular player for a long time, his opportunity to play decreased in 1997. In 1997, he moved to Japan Football League club Kawasaki Frontale. Toward end of his career, he played for Nagoya Grampus Eight (1998–1999) and Omiya Ardija (2000). He retired at the end of the 2000 season. On August 6, 1995, Noguchi debuted for the Japan national team against Costa Rica.

Koji Gyotoku is a former Japanese professional athlete. He is best known as an association football player and manager. From 2008 to 2009, he was manager of Bhutan's national football team. Gyotoku played for each of the schools he attended before he reached professional level.

Koji Miyata is a former Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Miyata was born on January 15, 1923. After graduating from Waseda University, he joined Tanabe Pharmaceutical in 1946. In March 1951, Miyata was selected Japan national team for Japan team first game after World War II, 1951 Asian Games. At this competition, on March 7, he debuted against Iran. He also played at 1954 Asian Games. He played 6 games for Japan until 1954. After retirement, Miyata became a manager for Tanabe Pharmaceutical in 1961. The club joined Japanese Regional Leagues in 1968 and was promoted to new division Japan Soccer League Division 2 in 1972. In 1972 season, he led the club the 2nd place and promoted Division 1. However, in 1973 season, the club was the lowest place and he resigned end of 1973 season. On January 15, 2023, Miyata turned 100 years old.

Koji Sasaki is a former Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Sasaki was born on January 30, 1936. After graduating from Kansai University, he joined Dunlop Japan in 1958. On December 25, 1958, he debuted for the Japan national team against Hong Kong. He played 14 games and scored 1 goal for Japan until 1961.

Koji Funamoto is a former Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Funamoto was born in Hiroshima on August 12, 1942. After graduating from Hiroshima University High School, he joined his local club, Toyo Industries in 1961. In 1965, Toyo Industries joined new league Japan Soccer League. The club won league champions in 1965, 1966, 1967, 1968 and 1970. The club also won 1965, 1967 and 1969 Emperor's Cup. He retired in 1975. He played all 166 league matches in 11 seasons. He was selected Best Eleven in 1970. In September 1967, Funamoto was selected the Japan national team for 1968 Summer Olympics qualification. At this qualification, he debuted against Philippines on September 27. However he was not selected the Japan for 1968 Summer Olympics. In 1970, he also played at 1970 Asian Games. He played 19 games for Japan until 1975.

Koji Alexander Murofushi is a Japanese athlete. He is best known as a hammer thrower who took part in four Summer Olympic Games. Murofushi was born in Numazu, Shizuoka Prefecture. His family were international sports competitors. His early interest in the hammer was encouarged by his father, Shigenobu Murofushi, who is an Olympic athlete and Asian Games champion. He is the brother of Yuka Murofushi, who is also an Olympian. Murofushi won the gold medal in the hammer throw at the 2004 Summer Olympics in Athens. He won the bronze medal at the 2012 Summer Olympics in London.

Koke (born Jorge Resurección Meredio in Madrid on 8 January 1992) is a Spanish footballer. He plays as a midfielder for Atlético Madrid. He played for the Spain national football team at the 2012 Summer Olympics in London.

Koji Kondo was a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Kondo was born in Kariya on April 28, 1972. After graduating from Shizuoka Gakuen High School, he joined Matsushita Electric (later Gamba Osaka) in 1991. From 1992, he played as regular player at many positions, midfielder and side-back. However at 1996 Emperor's Cup on December 29, he hit his head with opponent. A brain tumor was found by the examination. This match became his last match. He left the club in June 1998. He played 133 games and scored 4 goals in the league. On May 22, 1994, Kondo debuted for the Japan national team against Australia. He played as right side-back. On May 29, he also played against France. He played 2 games for Japan in 1994. On April 17, 2003, Kondo died of brain tumor in Toyoake at the age of 30.

At Final Battle, Komander won the Survival of the Fittest match to become the new ROH World Television Champion.

Konosuke Takeshita is a Japanese professional wrestler. He currently wrestles for All Elite Wrestling (AEW). He is a member of the Don Callis Family stable. Takeshita has also competed in DDT Pro-Wrestling (DDT), New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW), Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL), and on the independent circuit in Deadlock Pro-Wrestling (DPW). Takeshita has won many championships over his career. In AEW, Takeshita has been a one-time AEW International Champion. In DDT, he was a four-time Ironman Heavymetalweight Champion, five-time KO-D 6-Man Tag Team Champion, five-time KO-D Openweight Champion, four-time KO-D Tag Team Champion, and the winner of the KO-D Openweight Championship Challenger Decision Tournament in 2017, the KO-D Tag Team Championship Tournament in 2015, the D-Oh Grand Prix in 2019, 2021 II, the King of DDT Tournament in 2019 and 2021, and the Ultimate Tag League tournament in 2021 with Shunma Katsumata. In NJPW, he was a one-time NEVER Openweight Champion. On the April 12, 2021 episode of AEW Dark: Elevation, Takeshita made his AEW debut where he deleted Danny Limelight. He then traveled back to Japan to continue wrestling for DDT Pro-Wrestling (DDT). On the April 25, 2022 episode of AEW Dark: Elevation, Takeshita made his return to AEW and defeated Brandon Cutler. On the May 6 episode of Rampage, Takeshita faced Jay Lethal but lost because of interference from Sonjay Dutt and Satnam Singh. On the May 18 episode of Dynamite, Takeshita wrestled AEW World Champion "Hangman" Adam Page. While Takeshita did not win the match, it praised and was very well received. At Fyter Fest, Takeshita lost to Jon Moxley in a AEW Interim World Championship Eliminator Match. If he won, Takeshita earned a chance to challenge for Moxley's AEW World Championship in the future. At Battle of the Belts III, Takeshita challenged Claudio Castagnoli for his ROH World Championship but lost. On November 19, AEW owner Tony Khan announced that Takeshita signed a contract to become a member of the roster. At Double or Nothing, Takeshita turned heel and attacked Kenny Omega after The Elite's Anarchy in the Arena match, joining Don Callis and creating the Don Callis Family. On the May 31 episode of Rampage, Takeshita defeated Penta El Zero Miedo in qualifying match to challenge for the AEW TNT Title at Forbidden Door. At Forbidden Door, he wrestled in a ladder match for the vacant AEW TNT Championship but the match was won by Jack Perry. At All Out, Takeshita wrestled in a four-way match for Kazuchika Okada's AEW Continental Championship but Okada retained. At WrestleDream, Takeshita won a three-way match against Will Ospreay and Ricochet to win the AEW International Championship. This was Takeshita's first championship in AEW. At Revolution, Takeshita lost the title to Kenny Omega.

Konsta Helenius (born 11 May 2006) is a Finnish professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Buffalo Sabres of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Helenius played for Jukurit of the Liiga. Before playing in the NHL, Helenius played two seasons with the Jukurit of the Liiga. He was drafted 14th overall by the Buffalo Sabres in the 2024 NHL entry draft. On 8 July 2024, Helenius signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Sabres. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Rochester Americans. On 4 October 2018, the Sabres called him up and Helenius made his NHL debut in a 2–1 loss against the Carolina Hurricanes. On 13 October, Helenius recorded his first two points after assisting on goals from Noah Östlund and also scored his first NHL goal against Antti Raanta in a 5–3 win against the Nashville Predators.

Konstantina Kouteli (born 10 April 1981) is a Greek female water polo player. She was part of the Greek women's national water polo team at the 2006 Women's European Water Polo Championship, 2006 FINA Women's Water Polo World Cup, and 2009 World Aquatics Championships.

Konstantinos Zappas (; 1814–1892) was a Greek businessman who together with his cousin, Evangelos Zappas, revived the modern Olympic Games. Zappas was born to a Greek family in 1814 in the village of Labovo in the Ottoman Empire. After Evangelos Zappas died, Konstantinos took care of his cousin's legacy and the ongoing restoration of the Olympic Games. He was appointed manager of the Olympic Committee that organised the Zappas Olympics, the forerunner of the modern international Olympics. Konstantinos donated to a number of Greek schools including female schools in Constantinople. Zappas died in 1892 in Mantes-la-Jolie, France. After he died, the Romanian government took all of his assets in Romania causing a noted international law case. The statues of Konstantinos and his cousin Evangelos are located in front of the Zappeion Culture and Exhibition Center in Athens, Greece.

Korie Homan (born 16 June 1986, de Wijk) is a retired Dutch wheelchair tennis player. Homan was part of the current Paralympic doubles champion team. Homan is the former Australian Open Champion. She has won all the Grand Slam doubles titles. In 2009 she complete the Grand Slam with Esther Vergeer. In 2011 Homan retired from playing because of a wrist injury. Homan was born to Jan and Gina Willem. Homan has two older sisters. At the age of 12 Homan was involved in a car accident. In 2003, when she finished school she had her leg cut off (amputated) Homan first appeared on the wheelchair tennis tour in 2003. By the end of the season she had reached number 23. Homan did not have a ranking at the start of the year. In 2004 at the age of 17 Homan won her first Masters title. She won the doubles with Jiske Griffioen. At the 2005 US Open Homan reached her first Grand Slam finals. She reached both the singles and the doubles final. In the singles she lost in straight sets to Vergeer. But she won the doubles with Vergeer. In 2006 Homan won her first two series one titles. She won both the singles and doubles titles in Livorno. Homan also reached her second Grand Slam doubles final. At the US Open Maaike Smit was her team mate. They lost in straight sets to Vergeer and Griffioen. The pair also lost the final of the Masters. Homan started 2007 by losing in the final of the Australian Open doubles. Her partner in the event was Florence Gravellier. They lost the final in a match tiebreaker. At the US Open Homan was joined by Sharon Walraven. The pair reached the final before losing. Homan also had final defeats at the Super Series events of the British, Japan and US Opens. Homan lost both finals at the Masters. In 2008 Homan lost both the singles and doubles finals at the Australian and French Opens. She also lost in the singles final at the Masters. At the Paralympic Games Homan won a Gold Medal in the doubles event. She also won a silver medal in the singles. In the final she became the first player in over five years to hold match point against Vergeer. Homan's last competition was the 2010 Australian Open. In July 2011 Homan said that she had retired because of a wrist injury. Homan has a degree in biomedical science. As of September 2010, she is studying Veterinary Medicine.
